title: Goal-link dedupe runs AFTER the migration it must precede; DBs with duplicate NULL-slot links can no longer upgrade past 0023
description:
0023 runs `UPDATE goal_links SET slot = '' WHERE slot IS NULL` and then makes `slot` NOT NULL. The unique constraint `uq_goal_links_goal_entity_relation_slot` over `(goal_id, entity_type, entity_id, relation, slot)` has existed since 0022; because SQLite/Postgres treat NULLs as distinct in UNIQUE constraints, two goal_links rows that share goal/entity/relation but both have slot=NULL are legal at rest. The moment 0023's UPDATE sets both to '' it violates that unique constraint and the whole upgrade aborts. Commit 4ac4ddb ('move goal link dedupe to forward migration', bead rjg1.13) REMOVED the `_dedupe_unslotted_goal_links()` call that previously ran inside 0023 *before* this UPDATE, and put it in a new revision 0041 that sits LATER in the chain (0023 -> 0024 -> ... -> 0040 -> 0041). The dedupe therefore can never run before the statement that fails. I reproduced this end-to-end: seeding a DB at rev 0022 with two NULL-slot duplicate links and running `alembic upgrade head` fails with `IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: goal_links.goal_id, goal_links.entity_type, goal_links.entity_id, goal_links.relation, goal_links.slot` at the 0023 UPDATE. Consequence: any self-hosted DB currently at version <= 0022 that contains duplicate unslotted goal_links (possible in older DBs created before the slot default, or via direct SQL/imports) becomes permanently un-upgradeable, and since the app runs `alembic upgrade head` on startup this is a hard, data-blocking outage with no in-product recovery.

Fix: Restore the dedupe so it executes before 0023's slot-normalizing UPDATE. Simplest: re-add the `_dedupe_unslotted_goal_links()` DELETE as the first statement of 0023.upgrade() (before the UPDATE). If keeping a separate forward-only revision is desired for already-migrated DBs, that is fine to ALSO keep at 0041 for idempotency, but the in-0023 dedupe is required to keep stuck-at-0022 DBs upgradeable. The DELETE is already idempotent (it only removes ROW_NUMBER()>1 duplicates), so running it in both places is safe.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding migrations-1
close_reason: Implemented with focused regression coverage

title: SQLite backup + one-command restore (durability — highest leverage)
description: Eliminate the only unrecoverable-data-loss scenario. Add backup-on-startup in the serve path (cli.py) before alembic upgrade head, plus lab-tracker backup / lab-tracker restore CLI verbs. Correctness musts: WAL is ON (db.py:41) so a naive file copy can miss committed data in the -wal file — use the sqlite3 online-backup API (Connection.backup) or VACUUM INTO. Write at least one copy OFF the live disk/sync folder (backup --to <path> / documented destination) or the backup dies in the same rm/corruption/OneDrive-sync failure it is meant to survive. Prune old snapshots (keep last N); restore must refuse to clobber a live/locked DB.
acceptance_criteria: Backup produces a valid standalone DB while the app is running under WAL; restore refuses to overwrite without confirmation; old snapshots pruned; supports an off-host destination.
notes: Deep review 2026-06-19 independently confirmed this as a HIGH durability gap (finding sweep-integrity-2): the Dolt mirror is export-only and lossy; SQLite deployments have no recovery path. See docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-19.md.

title: Client _list_all total-cap regression breaks upsert idempotency / evidence dedup past 200 rows
description: src/lab_tracker_client/client.py:838-874. _list_all was redefined from page-size to a hard TOTAL cap; every natural-key finder (find_project_by_name, find_question_by_text, find_note_by_marker, find_evidence_note, build_evidence_note_index) calls list_*(limit=MAX_PAGE_SIZE=200) and both client (_validate_limit) and server (validate_pagination) cap a scan at 200. In any project with >200 notes/projects/questions, an existing record past row 200 is invisible, so upsert_* POSTs a duplicate and lt-import-folder re-imports already-captured evidence on every re-sync. No server-side uniqueness constraint on the evidence key exists, so dedup is purely client-side. Introduced this batch (c1u.8); the new test only pins the cap, no multi-page finder test exists. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Add an unbounded _iter_all generator that pages until offset>=total; finders use it instead of list_*(limit=200). Keep limit-as-cap only for public bounded reads. Add a finder test with >200 rows proving a record past offset 200 is found and not duplicated.

title: Non-technical onboarding: make Lab Tracker usable by bench scientists & PIs without a terminal
description:
Lab Tracker's stated audience is wet-lab bench scientists and PIs (README.md:17-19), but every documented path to a running app is a developer/terminal workflow. An audit (2026-06-15) found there is no hosted URL, no GUI installer, and no download-and-run path: the first Quickstart instruction is `uv venv` (README.md:24), the GitHub repo has an empty homepageUrl and zero releases, and the realistic shared-lab path is 15+ terminal commands across up to 7 tools (uv/Python, Node/npm, Docker, Postgres, Dolt, Beads).

Key finding: the wall is SETUP/DEPLOYMENT, not day-to-day clicking. Once someone technical stands up a server, a non-technical scientist CAN reach the browser/phone PWA and log in — but no one in a typical wet lab can do that setup unaided, and several end-user dead-ends remain (read-only self-registration, no onboarding, admin bootstrap only via raw HTTP POST).

This epic groups the docs, launcher, deployment, and in-app onboarding work that lowers the barrier so a bench scientist/PI can evaluate and use Lab Tracker without engineering support. Children are tagged [quick-win] / [medium] / [larger] by effort in their titles.
acceptance_criteria: A PI can evaluate the product without a build (hosted demo or screenshots); a lab member who is "the techy one" can stand up a shared instance with roughly one command and create the first admin + invite members from a UI; a bench scientist can reach phone capture and write notes after being given a link + login.
close_reason: Completed non-technical onboarding epic: README now starts with a hosted read-only demo, screenshots, scientist-start guidance, Render one-click deploy, desktop/local launchers, LAN phone helper, browser first-admin setup, admin user management/invites, managed deploy docs, and the stable public demo verified at https://samuelbrudner.github.io/lab-tracker/app/.

title: Fix portfolio last_activity_at tz-aware/naive HTTP 500 + graph-change-set regression test
description: GET /portfolio/summary returns HTTP 500 for any accessible project that has a graph change set. _latest_activity_at (src/lab_tracker/routes/portfolio.py:122-143) builds a candidate list of tz-aware datetimes (project plus eight entity mappers normalize via as_utc) then calls max(), but change_set_from_model (src/lab_tracker/sqlalchemy_repository_parts/graph_drafts.py:199-200) returns created_at/updated_at WITHOUT as_utc normalization. On SQLite (all tests and local dev) DateTime(timezone=True) returns tz-naive datetimes, so max() over mixed aware/naive raises TypeError. Postgres masks it. Existing tests never create a change set, so it is latent.
design: Defensively normalize each non-None timestamp with as_utc inside _activity_timestamps before max(); additionally normalize change_set_from_model for parity with the other eight mappers (the underlying c1u.5 fix). Add a portfolio route test that creates a graph change set and asserts 200 + correct last_activity_at.
acceptance_criteria: GET /portfolio/summary returns 200 for a project with a graph change set on SQLite; regression test added; change_set_from_model normalized.
notes: Net-new portfolio-specific surface; cross-links lab-tracker-c1u.5 (mapper normalization). Fixing c1u.5 alone resolves the crash but not the route-level guard or the test.
close_reason: Normalized graph-draft timestamps and added portfolio regression coverage

title: PI information organization: project groups, people-edges, and portfolio views
description: A PI deploys Lab Tracker with many projects and project-scoped trainees. Today there is no container above Project, no real notion of people (created_by is a free string; the only cross-project tier is global ADMIN), and oversight requires being a global admin. This epic adds an organizing-edge layer — a Lab/project-group container, supervision and ownership edges, and read-only portfolio/lab-health views — without becoming an identity provider, HR system, or grants-management product. Build-vs-buy moat preserved: identity stays offloadable; we own the semantic edges.
design:
CONCEPT: Add the three semantic edges no identity provider models — group ownership, supervision, attribution — onto the existing model; route PI oversight through accessible_project_ids(). No org-chart/HR/IdP/grants-management.

NEW: project_groups (kind=lab) + group_memberships (reuse VIEWER/CONTRIBUTOR/OWNER enum); supervision_edges (dated, own table keyed by user_id, NOT a users column); shadow FK created_by_user_id/executed_by_user_id (additive; string stays, dual-written).
CHANGE: goals.project_id nullable + GoalLink EntityType.PROJECT slot (enum value already exists, models.py:155); accessible_project_ids()/membership_role() group-aware.
REUSE: prov:Agent -> prov:Person/wasAttributedTo/actedOnBehalfOf (export-only); project_graph, decision_context (stays single-project), graph-draft human review, goals.

ACCESS CONTRACT (2.1, asymmetric): group OWNER inherits OWNER on every child project (PI oversight w/o global admin); group VIEWER/CONTRIBUTOR inherit NOTHING unless an explicit per-group group_read_all flag (default false). Direct project membership resolves first; admin short-circuit and >=1-owner-per-project guard untouched.

BOUNDARY: every new edge points at the offloadable users table but adds NO domain column to users itself. Aggregations (portfolio/lab-health) read only over the in-house question/claim/goal graph — not a metrics/ELN dashboard.

PHASES: 0 read-only portfolio (zero schema) -> 1 group container + group-aware access -> 2 attribution FK (isolated) -> 3 spanning goals + supervision + PROV-O people -> 4 offboarding export + ownership reassignment. Each additive, single Alembic head.

Source: multi-agent design pass (2026-06-15), grounded in db_models.py, services/project_authorization.py, auth.py, provenance.py, docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md, docs/retained-v1-surface.md.
DEFERRED per PI decision (2026-06-15): co-PI / cross-lab / multi-parented projects. Single-parent projects.group_id stands; co-PI handled later by direct per-project membership + goal-level overlap if demand proves it.
NOTE: per-trainee attribution has signal only once multi-user auth (auth_enabled=True) is in use; default local mode collapses all rows to one ADMIN user.

title: Build-vs-buy: define Lab Tracker responsibility boundaries vs existing tools
description: Lab Tracker's durable product is the PROV-O / JSON-LD semantic provenance spine threading questions -> notes -> sessions -> datasets -> analyses -> claims -> visualizations (see src/lab_tracker/provenance.py). It is anchored by two node types no external tool provides: Questions (broad-to-atomic inquiry structure) and Claims (epistemic layer linking evidence to conclusions with confidence). Many adjacent responsibilities are either commodity infrastructure or owned by mature tool categories that Lab Tracker risks accidentally half-reimplementing: identity/RBAC, byte/asset storage, data versioning, experiment tracking, note capture (ELNs), transcription, and search. This epic decomposes the boundary decisions: for each adjacent responsibility decide offload / integrate-via-adapter / build-in-house, so effort concentrates on the irreducible semantic core. Already-resolved boundaries: voice transcription is offloaded to an explicit note-scoped action (retained-v1); multimodal note-to-graph extraction is offloaded to the LLM while the human-gated draft->commit diff stays in-house; semantic/vector search is explicitly deferred in retained-v1.
design: Shared principle - pointer-not-reimplementation: for each adjacent responsibility, store a reference (URI + content hash) to the external tool's artifact PLUS the semantic edges the external tool does not model (which question a dataset addresses, which claim an analysis supports). Do not reimplement the external tool's core. The PROV-O export is the integration seam: ingest external artifacts (DVC/DataLad manifests, MLflow runs, ELN entries) as PROV entities and connect them to inquiry and claims. Integrate decisions should strengthen the core by letting it focus on the semantic graph, not shrink it. Danger zone: each integrate decision is a slippery slope toward rebuilding half of MLflow or half of an ELN - resist field-by-field creep past a reference + edges.
acceptance_criteria: Each child decision reaches a recorded outcome (offload / integrate-via-adapter / build-in-house / defer) with rationale, a concrete integration seam or boundary description, and follow-up implementation issues filed where needed. The retained-v1 surface doc (docs/retained-v1-surface.md) and architecture notes are updated to reflect chosen boundaries. Tool-landscape names are validated as current before committing to any one.
close_reason: Completed build-vs-buy boundary epic: all six child decisions recorded and closed, follow-up adapter/storage issues filed, retained-v1 and internal boundary docs updated, PROV-O ingestion seam implemented with dataset external-artifact round-trip coverage, pytest and Ruff passed.

title: Make request lifecycle context-managed
description: Replace finish_request(committed=...) and middleware-level mutable commit flags with a context-managed request lifecycle. The current caller must remember whether a database session committed before deferred after-commit or after-rollback hooks run, which is easy to misuse on exception or rollback paths.
design: Introduce a request-scope/context-manager API that owns repository binding, commit/rollback outcome, deferred-action dispatch, and cleanup. The FastAPI database middleware should enter the request scope, run the handler, commit or roll back through one explicit lifecycle path, and let the scope fire after_commit only after a successful commit and after_rollback only on rollback/error. Keep public route and LabTrackerAPI behavior unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: finish_request(committed=...) is removed or reduced to a non-public compatibility shim that no caller must use. Middleware no longer tracks a mutable committed flag to decide deferred hooks. after_commit hooks run only after a successful commit; after_rollback hooks run on rollback/error paths. Route/session tests cover successful commit and rollback/error behavior. Backend tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented context-managed request lifecycle; removed finish_request(committed=...) and middleware committed flag; added exception rollback hook regression coverage. title: Replace LabTrackerAPI service mixins with composed services
description: Replace the LabTrackerAPI inheritance facade with explicit service objects while preserving the current flat LabTrackerAPI public method surface. The current class inherits many service mixins that implicitly share repository, raw storage, and request context through self, which hides dependencies and makes service-level unit testing difficult.
design: Introduce a ServiceContext that carries the active repository/unit-of-work, raw storage, request context, and any shared service helpers. Convert *ServiceMixin classes into normal service classes that receive this context and any explicit service dependencies via constructors. LabTrackerAPI remains a thin compatibility facade exposing the existing flat methods used by routes, MCP paths, and tests; it delegates internally to composed services. Split singleton/root API construction from request-scoped API construction where practical so repository/request-context availability is enforced by types or constructors instead of runtime optional checks. Replace lambda-passing repository writes with an explicit unit-of-work/context-manager style in the new services rather than carrying _run_repository_write(lambda repository: ...) forward.
acceptance_criteria: Service dependencies are explicit in constructors instead of hidden through mixin inheritance. LabTrackerAPI continues to expose the current flat method names and existing route/MCP behavior remains unchanged. Request-scoped and singleton/root construction paths are represented by distinct types or otherwise made explicit. Representative services can be unit-tested without instantiating the full facade. New service write paths use an explicit unit-of-work/context-manager pattern rather than lambda-passed repository operations. Backend tests pass.
close_reason: Composed LabTrackerAPI services behind the flat facade; converted service mixins to explicit services with ServiceContext/unit_of_work; added service composition tests. Gates: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_service_composition.py -q (4 passed), .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q (266 passed), .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m ruff check . (passed).

title: Retire dual in-memory/repository runtime
description: Remove the parallel InMemoryStore path and make LabTrackerAPI/service reads and writes use the repository path unconditionally. The current dual runtime keeps a dict-backed store and SQLAlchemy repository active in the same process, forcing every read/write through cache/repository branching and whole-store hydration after failed writes.
design: Delete InMemoryStore, hydrate_from_repository, _uses_in_memory_entity_cache, _get_cached_entity, and repository/store branching from API and services. Tests that need fast feedback should use repository-backed SQLite fixtures rather than the parallel dict store. Preserve the retained-v1 public behavior and API method names while simplifying persistence internally.
acceptance_criteria: No parallel dict store remains in runtime code. Reads and writes go through LabTrackerRepository-backed persistence. Existing API behavior is unchanged for retained-v1 workflows. Tests that previously depended on InMemoryStore use repository-backed fixtures. Backend tests pass.
close_reason: Repository-only LabTrackerAPI runtime implemented; in-memory store removed and tests migrated to SQLite repository helper.

title: Epic: Architecture cleanup from code-quality review
description:
Own the architecture cleanup roadmap from the code-quality review. The review identified two high-leverage structural problems, the LabTrackerAPI mixin facade and the dual in-memory/repository runtime, plus several medium-sized module and validation cleanup tracks.

This epic is issue-tracker work only. It should coordinate incremental refactors while preserving the retained-v1 runtime surface and avoiding changes to Lab Tracker research records.
design: Map review P0 items to bead priority 1; reserve bead priority 0 for broken builds, security, or data loss. Keep product feature beads independent unless implementation later proves a direct dependency. Child beads should be small enough to land as separate PRs with tests.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for the dual runtime, service composition, graph draft split, MCP split, mapper decision, status transition cleanup, Pydantic validation migration, authorization policy, app factory split, and small review nits. Dependencies show the hard sequencing constraints. No code or research-record changes are required by this epic itself.
close_reason: Completed all architecture cleanup child beads from the code-quality review. All 13 subtasks are closed, retained-v1 behavior was preserved through the final app-factory split, and the final child gates passed: focused app/auth/db/frontend tests, full pytest, and Ruff.

title: Dolt mirror: unresolvable FK cycle between graph_change_sets and notes
description:
pytest emits SAWarning at src/lab_tracker/dolt_mirror.py:74: 'Cannot correctly sort tables; there are unresolvable cycles between tables graph_change_sets, notes, usually caused by mutually dependent foreign key constraints. Foreign key constraints involving these tables will not be considered; this warning may raise an error in a future release.' The Dolt mirror may order/handle graph_change_sets and notes incorrectly during export, and a future SQLAlchemy upgrade turns this warning into a hard error.

Fix: Break the FK cycle (e.g. use_alter=True on one of the mutually-dependent FKs) or give dolt_mirror an explicit table ordering instead of relying on SQLAlchemy's topological sort.

title: Entire test suite runs only on SQLite while production targets Postgres - cross-backend FK/cascade/isolation behavior is untested
description:
All integration fixtures build SQLite URLs (sqlite_database_url / migrated_sqlite_database_url, conftest.py:100-121) and there is no Postgres-backed test path, yet CLAUDE.md and the skills describe a 'Postgres live runtime' as the deployment target. The cross-cutting integrity behaviors that differ between the two engines are precisely the ones this area cares about: ON DELETE cascade/RESTRICT ordering within multi-child cascades, FK enforcement semantics, the REPEATABLE READ isolation branch in the Dolt export (dolt_mirror.py:86-87, which is skipped on SQLite and therefore never exercised), default-NO-ACTION vs RESTRICT timing for datasets.primary_question_id / sessions.primary_question_id (db_models.py:194-198, 559-562), and JSON/boolean column round-tripping. Consequence: a schema or delete-ordering change could pass CI on SQLite and corrupt or fail on the actual Postgres deployment, with no automated signal.

Fix: Add a Postgres-parametrized variant of the integration fixtures (e.g. a marker/env-gated session that runs migrations + a representative subset of the cascade/delete/export tests against a Postgres container), at minimum covering project-cascade delete with full entity tree, the Dolt export REPEATABLE READ path, and FK enforcement. Run it in CI.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding sweep-integrity-3
close_reason: Added env-gated Postgres integration subset and CI service job for migrations, FK/cascade, Dolt export, JSON/boolean coverage

title: Deleting an analysis orphans goal_links pointing at its cascade-deleted visualizations
description:
goal_links reference targets by plain (entity_type, entity_id) columns with NO foreign key (db_models.py:854-855), so they are never removed by DB cascade and must be pruned in application code. delete_analysis (analysis_service.py:248-254) calls remove_goal_links_to_entity for the ANALYSIS only, then deletes the analysis row. The DB then cascade-deletes that analysis's visualizations (visualizations.analysis_id ForeignKey ondelete='CASCADE', db_models.py:877). Any goal_link whose target is (VISUALIZATION, viz_id) for those cascade-deleted visualizations is left behind, pointing at a row that no longer exists. VISUALIZATION is a valid goal target (models.py:248). Consequence: goals silently accumulate dangling links to deleted figures; goal-scope invariants (a projectless goal must retain a real target) can be violated, and downstream goal/portfolio queries surface phantom entities. Note the project-delete path is correct here (remove_goal_links_to_project_contents enumerates visualizations, goal_link_cleanup.py:38-53) - only the direct analysis-delete path has the gap, which is exactly the kind of inconsistency that hides in review.

Fix: In delete_analysis, before deleting, enumerate the analysis's visualizations (repository.query_visualizations(... ) filtered to analysis_id, or the existing viz lookup) and build a target set that includes both (ANALYSIS, analysis_id) and (VISUALIZATION, viz_id) for each child, then call remove_goal_links_to_targets(repository, targets) once. Add a regression test that links a goal to a visualization, deletes the parent analysis, and asserts the goal_link is gone.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding sweep-integrity-1
close_reason: Removed goal links for analysis visualizations before cascade delete

title: Note raw-asset capture writes are not fsync'd or atomically replaced
description:
LocalNoteStorage.store_stream writes the captured bytes directly to the final path via path.open('wb') (line 62-70) and store/_write_bytes uses path.write_bytes (line 105-108); neither fsyncs the file nor uses a temp-file + os.replace. The note DB row (which references the storage_id) is committed by SQLite, but the asset bytes may not be durably flushed to disk, so after a power loss the DB can claim a note exists while its raw asset is truncated or missing. The non-atomic write also leaves a partial/orphaned file at the final path on a crash mid-write. Notably the sibling dataset/visualization backend (file_storage.py:_atomic_write_bytes and store_stream lines 164-175) already does fsync + os.replace, so the capture path -- which holds the often-only copy of an irreplaceable phone capture -- has strictly weaker durability than the dataset path.

Fix: Mirror LocalFileStorageBackend: write to a NamedTemporaryFile in the same directory, handle.flush() + os.fsync(handle.fileno()), then os.replace onto the final path, cleaning up the temp file on failure. This gives atomic publish and crash durability for note raw assets.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding sweep-concurrency-4
close_reason: Made raw note storage writes atomic and fsync-backed with cleanup coverage

title: Scheduled batch runner has no overlap/double-run protection
description:
run_due_graph_draft_batches selects due settings via list_due (graph_batches.py:184-194, a plain SELECT on enabled AND next_run_at<=now) and only advances next_run_at AFTER each project's run completes (line 624-633). The run itself includes a slow LLM call, so the due window stays open for seconds. The whole thing runs inside one request-managed transaction (RepositoryUnitOfWork does not commit when request-managed, base.py:79-80), so the RUNNING GraphDraftBatchRun row created at graph_draft_service.py:519-520 is never committed mid-run and is invisible to any concurrent caller. Two concurrent POSTs to /batches/run-due (or one cron whose interval is shorter than the run, or an admin manually triggering while cron runs) will both see the same project as due and both invoke run_graph_draft_batch_for_project. Because each invocation computes window_end from its own current_time, the two batch_keys can differ, so both runs execute a full LLM batch draft and write separate change sets / runs for the same notes; when batch_keys do match, the loser hits the uncaught uq_graph_draft_batch_runs_batch_key IntegrityError and 500s.

Fix: Claim each due settings row atomically before running: issue an UPDATE ... SET next_run_at=<next> WHERE settings_id=? AND next_run_at=<observed> and only run the project if rowcount==1 (advance the schedule up front, not after). Alternatively serialize run-due with a single-flight guard / advisory lock so only one invocation processes due projects at a time, and commit the RUNNING row before the LLM call so concurrent callers can see it.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding sweep-concurrency-2
close_reason: Added atomic due-settings claim before scheduled batch drafting with regression coverage

title: Capture upload retry creates duplicate notes (no idempotency key)
description:
The offline upload queue replays capture POSTs to /notes/quick-capture and /notes/upload-file with no idempotency token, and the server (routes/notes.py:86-162 -> upload_note_raw) performs no dedup. Two failure modes produce duplicates: (1) a network error thrown by fetch AFTER the server already created the note but before the response reached the phone (flaky LAN/Wi-Fi, dropped connection) leaves the item queued (results.stillQueued.push at line 230) and it is retried on the next drain; (2) any 5xx (e.g. a 502/504 from a reverse proxy issued after the note was committed) hits the else branch at line 265-267 and is likewise retried. Each replay creates a brand-new note row AND a new on-disk raw asset. This is exactly the flaky-network scenario the queue exists for, so duplicate staged notes (and wasted irreplaceable-capture storage) are a realistic outcome that also pollutes the daily batch-draft window.

Fix: Generate a client-side idempotency key per enqueued item (e.g. a UUID stored in the IndexedDB record at enqueue time) and send it as a form field / header on every retry. On the server, add a unique constraint on (project_id, client_capture_id) for notes and have upload_note_raw look up an existing note by that key, returning the existing note (200) instead of inserting a duplicate when the key is already present.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding sweep-concurrency-1
close_reason: Added capture idempotency keys across note uploads and offline queue retries

title: Acquisition watcher re-hashes every file on every poll (expensive hash runs before the cheap stat check)
description:
In scan(), `_stable_fingerprint(file_path)` is called for EVERY file on EVERY poll BEFORE the cheap size/mtime short-circuit at lines 80-85. `_stable_fingerprint` (line 125-138) calls `_hash_file` (line 128), which reads the entire file and computes SHA-256. The size/mtime comparison against the cached fingerprint that would skip unchanged files only happens AFTER the full hash has already been computed. For the watcher's actual use case (instrument output directories that can hold many multi-GB files), this means the process re-reads and SHA-256s every file on the watch tree at every interval (default 1s in run(), line 105). This is an O(total bytes) cost per poll and will saturate disk I/O / CPU and effectively make the watcher unusable on large acquisition datasets. The cheap stat check is meant to gate the expensive hash, but the order is inverted.

Fix: Restructure scan() to stat first and hash only when needed: read `path.stat()`, compare size+mtime against `self._fingerprints[file_path]`; if both match a previously-registered fingerprint, `continue` without hashing. Only when size/mtime differ (or no prior fingerprint) compute the stable hash. Keep the stability double-stat inside the hash branch. This preserves change detection while bounding per-poll cost to a stat() per file for the steady state.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding storage-1
close_reason: Moved watcher hash behind cached stat check with regression coverage

title: delete_session destroys provenance: no guard against deleting a session referenced as a committed dataset's source_session_id
description:
delete_session removes the session and (via the acquisition_outputs.session_id ondelete=CASCADE FK at db_models.py:602) silently cascade-deletes every registered acquisition output, with no reference check. Meanwhile a dataset created by promote_operational_session_to_dataset records the session in commit_manifest.source_session_id, which is persisted as a plain String(36) column (db_models.py:208) with NO foreign key. So you can delete an operational session after it has been promoted to a committed dataset: the dataset keeps a source_session_id pointing at a now-nonexistent session, and the acquisition outputs that back that committed dataset's file manifest vanish. For a tool whose stated purpose is preserving research provenance, this silently breaks the provenance chain for irreplaceable committed data. Contrast delete_dataset (_ensure_dataset_can_be_deleted) and delete_question (_ensure_question_not_referenced), which both refuse deletion while referenced. test_session_routes.py only covers deleting an unreferenced session, so the gap is untested.

Fix: Before deleting a session, query datasets in the session's project (or add a repository lookup keyed on manifest_source_session_id) and raise ValidationError if any committed/non-staged dataset's commit_manifest.source_session_id == session_id, mirroring the reference guards on dataset/question deletion. Also consider guarding sessions that still have acquisition outputs. Add a regression test that promotes a session to a committed dataset and asserts the session cannot be deleted.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding services-crud-1
close_reason: Blocked deletion of sessions referenced by non-staged dataset manifests

title: Per-user record export and offboarding guard silently omit sessions and visualizations
description:
export_user_records()/_collect_records() return repository.records_attributed_to_user(), which yields a RecordExportRecords containing only questions, datasets, analyses, claims, claim_edges, and notes (models.py:876-883 has no sessions/visualizations fields). Sessions (project-scoped, created_by attributed; db_models.py:544-566) and Visualizations are first-class retained-v1 entities (docs/retained-v1-surface.md:39-45) and ARE attributed/reassigned by reassign() (ownership.py:60-64,77). The offboarding guard's _attributed_record_project_ids() (project_service.py:644-654) reads the same RecordExportRecords and likewise ignores sessions/visualizations. Consequences: (1) the two offboarding-release mechanisms diverge -- reassign moves session/viz attribution, but export does NOT preserve them, so an admin who 'export-then-revokes' loses the departing user's session and visualization provenance; (2) a departing user whose only attributable artifacts are sessions or visualizations passes _ensure_offboarding_records_released() with no export at all, then is revoked, leaving those rows attributed to a removed member. For an app whose entire purpose is preserving research reasoning, this is a real data-preservation defect.

Fix: Add sessions and visualizations to RecordExportRecords and to repository.records_attributed_to_user() (using SessionModel.created_by/created_by_user_id and VisualizationModel.created_by/created_by_user_id with the project_filter), include them in _record_counts() and in _project_ids_for_records(), and add their project_ids to _attributed_record_project_ids() in project_service so the offboarding guard blocks revoke until they are exported or reassigned. Add a regression test asserting a user with only a session/visualization is blocked from revoke until export.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding services-authz-1
close_reason: Implemented with focused regression coverage

title: Goal origin/revision edges in Ara logic layer reference nodes that are never materialized (dangling JSON-LD)
description:
In `_ara_logic_graph`, the goal node is added via `_goal_node(...)` (line 1317), which calls `_apply_origin_provenance` (provenance.py:1481). For a Goal with `origin == USER_REVISED` and a `change_set_id`, that helper emits `prov:wasRevisionOf` pointing at a `.../goals/<id>/versions/before/<change_set_id>` IRI and a `changeSet`/`prov:wasGeneratedBy` reference to the draft-activity IRI. Unlike every other entity type in this module (claims, datasets, analyses, questions, notes, visualizations — each of which pairs `_apply_origin_provenance` with a `_merge_graph_nodes(merged, _origin_provenance_nodes(...))` call), the goal branch never calls `_origin_provenance_nodes(base_url, records.goal)`. Goal also carries `origin`, `change_set_id`, `origin_provider`, `origin_model`, `origin_prompt_version` (models.py:824-828). Consequence: for any AI-suggested or AI-revised goal, the exported Ara logic layer contains dangling references — the draft `prov:Activity`, the `prov:SoftwareAgent` (with aiProvider/aiModel/aiPromptVersion), and the pre-revision 'before' `prov:Entity` are missing, so the JSON-LD graph is not self-consistent and the AI-origin attribution for the goal is silently lost. test_provenance.py:269 explicitly asserts this self-consistency invariant for visualizations but no equivalent test exists for goals.

Fix: After adding the goal node in `_ara_logic_graph`, mirror the other entity branches: `_merge_graph_nodes(merged, _origin_provenance_nodes(base_url, records.goal))`. Add a regression test that builds an Ara artifact for an AI_SUGGESTED/USER_REVISED goal and asserts the draft activity, software agent, and (for USER_REVISED) the before-revision node are all present in the logic-layer @graph.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding provenance-1
close_reason: Implemented with focused regression coverage

description:
Fix: Add a migration test that, at rev 0022, inserts two goal_links rows sharing (goal_id, entity_type, entity_id, relation) both with slot=NULL, then runs `command.upgrade(config, 'head')` and asserts it succeeds and that exactly one of the duplicate rows survives (the oldest by created_at/link_id, matching the ROW_NUMBER ORDER BY).

title: Write MCP tools have no error handling, so failures return a raw, unstructured error blob instead of the structured envelope read tools provide
description:
Every write tool (lab_tracker_create_project/question/note/dataset/analysis/claim/claim_edge/visualization/goal, update_goal, link_node_to_goal, upload_visualization_file, refactor_question, record_evidence_bundle) wraps the client call in only `try: ... finally: client.close()`. No except clause catches LabTrackerAPIError/LabTrackerAPIValidationError/LabTrackerAPIAuthError/LabTrackerAPIUnavailableError/httpx.HTTPError. By contrast, read tools route every call through _read_tool (src/lab_tracker/mcp_tools/read.py:40-53), which converts failures into the structured envelope produced by lab_tracker_unavailable / lab_tracker_api_error (error.code, status_code, issues, and a next_action hint the agent is instructed to follow). When a write fails, FastMCP catches the exception and re-raises ToolError (.venv mcp/server/fastmcp/tools/base.py:116-117), which the low-level server turns into a CallToolResult with isError=True and the bare string 'Error executing tool lab_tracker_create_claim: Lab Tracker request POST /claims failed: ...' (mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py:583-584). Consequence: on a write the agent loses error.code, the 422 `issues` list (field-level validation detail the client already parses in _append_issue_text), the auth-vs-unavailable distinction, and the next_action guidance — exactly the machine-actionable contract the read path is built around. For irreplaceable research data this makes write failures hard for the agent to recover from correctly (e.g. it cannot reliably tell 'fix your input' from 'service is down, stop retrying').

Fix: Introduce a shared _write_tool helper mirroring _read_tool: catch (LabTrackerAPIUnavailableError, httpx.HTTPError) -> lab_tracker_unavailable(tool_name, detail=...), and LabTrackerAPIError -> lab_tracker_api_error(tool_name, exc), wrapping the structured result with with_next_action, in a try/finally that closes the client. Route all WRITE_TOOLS through it so read and write surfaces return the same structured error envelope. Add tests asserting a failing write tool returns error.code/issues/next_action rather than raising.

title: Search-slice truncation is invisible: no was_truncated signal when matches exceed limit
description:
truncation() is computed only over the recency payloads (questions_payload, notes_payload, ...). The search_payload built by reader.search() reports meta.questions_count/notes_count as the number of RETURNED items (decision_context_query.py:201), not the total number of matches, and it is not included in the truncation list at all. Combined with the oldest-first ordering above, when a project has more matching questions/notes than `limit`, the response silently omits matches AND reports truncation.was_truncated=False for the search dimension. An assistant consuming this payload has no way to know relevant evidence was dropped, which is dangerous for a system whose explicit job is to prevent decisions made on incomplete context.

Fix: Have reader.search() return the true total match counts (query_questions/query_notes already return total) in meta, and include the search payload in the truncation() sections so was_truncated reflects dropped search matches. At minimum, surface a 'search' truncation section keyed off returned vs. total matches.

title: Search seam returns OLDEST matches first and drops newer ones (created_at ASC, no recent_first)
description:
RepositoryDecisionContextReader.search() calls query_questions()/query_notes() with a search pattern and a limit but does NOT pass recent_first. The underlying query (sqlalchemy_repository_parts/core.py:526-527 and notes.py:158-159) therefore defaults to ORDER BY created_at ASC, question_id ASC. So when a project has more matching questions/notes than `limit` (default 20, easy for a common term in a real lab), the 'search_match' slice returns the OLDEST matches and silently discards the most recent ones. This directly undermines the tool's purpose (surfacing the most relevant/current reasoning before a research decision) and the documented retrieval_policy 'explicit_links_then_search_then_recency'. The recency payloads correctly use recent_first=True, so the search slice is the odd one out and the two slices fight each other for the limited budget.

Fix: Pass recent_first=True (or add an updated_first ordering) to the query_questions/query_notes calls inside search() so the search slice surfaces the newest matches, consistent with the recency payloads. Alternatively expose ordering on the reader.search signature and have build_decision_context request recency ordering.

title: Usage-event retention silently creates duplicate rollup buckets, double-counting analytics (relates to telemetry retention lab-tracker-uk45.10 — the rollup must be idempotent)
description:
rollup_usage_events_before() always INSERTs a fresh-UUID UsageEventRollupModel for every bucket (session.add at line 283), never merging into an existing bucket. The retention endpoint POST /usage-events/retention/run uses a sliding cutoff (now - 365 days), so events from a single calendar day get rolled up across multiple daily runs, producing repeated buckets for the same (day, verb, resource_type, project_id, actor_role, principal_type, surface, outcome) key. The uq_usage_event_rollup_bucket UNIQUE constraint is supposed to prevent this, but it does NOT fire because the bucket includes nullable dimensions (project_id, actor_role, principal_type, surface) and SQL treats NULLs as distinct in UNIQUE constraints. Most usage events have a NULL project_id, so the common case silently inserts a duplicate bucket instead of raising. I reproduced this: two events on the same day rolled up in two runs yield two separate rollup rows each with event_count=1. Consequence: usage analytics become silently inflated/double-counted over time; aggregations over rollups overstate activity, with no error surfaced.

Fix: In rollup_usage_events_before, before inserting, look up an existing rollup row for the bucket key (using IS NULL comparisons for the nullable dimensions) and, if found, increment event_count/total_duration_ms/total_result_count on that row instead of adding a new one (mirroring SQLAlchemyUsageEventRollupRepository.save). Equivalently, route the merge through the rollup repo's upsert logic. Add a regression test that runs retention twice over events sharing a NULL-dimension bucket and asserts a single merged rollup row.

title: upsert_note silently discards new content when first non-blank line collides
description:
upsert_note derives an idempotency 'marker' from only the first non-blank line of the content (first_line_marker) and, if any existing note in the project shares that marker, returns the existing note WITHOUT sending the new content (line 630-632). Two genuinely different notes that happen to begin with the same heading/first line (e.g. '# Notes', '## Results', a shared template header) collapse: the caller believes the note was written but the new body is silently dropped and never persisted. This is the documented marker-based contract, but it is a sharp edge for irreplaceable lab notes and the test at tests/test_lab_tracker_client.py:103-107 demonstrates the silent drop ('Updated body that should not duplicate'). There is no signal to the caller distinguishing 'created' from 'matched existing and discarded your content'.

Fix: Make the outcome observable and the marker robust: either return a flag/field indicating reuse-vs-create (so callers can detect a no-op write), or require a stronger marker (e.g. an explicit idempotency key / content hash) rather than the bare first line. At minimum, document on the method that a first-line collision discards content, and consider warning/raising when an existing match's body differs from the supplied content.

title: serve --host 0.0.0.0 exposes an unauthenticated admin app to the LAN with no warning
description:
The serve subcommand accepts an arbitrary --host (default 127.0.0.1, which is safe) but does nothing to reconcile the bind interface with the auth posture. By default environment='local' (config.py:22) and Settings.is_auth_enabled() returns False for 'local' (config.py:54-57), so the auth middleware short-circuits and grants every request a full ADMIN local context (middleware.py:93-95, local_auth_context()). A user following the 'open to my lab' instinct who runs `lab_tracker serve --host 0.0.0.0` therefore publishes a fully unauthenticated, admin-privileged app onto the LAN, with read/write/delete over all irreplaceable research data, and the CLI prints no warning. serve_app only special-cases 0.0.0.0/:: for the *browser* URL (cli.py:80) and never checks whether binding a non-loopback interface while auth is disabled is dangerous.

Fix: In serve_app (or main()), detect a non-loopback host (anything other than 127.0.0.1/::1/localhost) and, when settings.is_auth_enabled() is False, refuse to start (raise SystemExit with a clear message) or require an explicit override flag like --insecure-allow-lan. At minimum emit a prominent stderr warning naming the exposed interface and the disabled-auth state. Read get_settings() in serve_app to make this decision before uvicorn.run.

title: Auth-refresh has no minimum-delay floor: short token TTL causes a /auth/refresh storm
description: src/lab_tracker/frontend_src/hooks/useAuthSession.js:187-215. scheduleRefresh uses Math.max(0, expiresAtMs - Date.now() - REFRESH_MARGIN_MS(5min)). description: src/lab_tracker/services/graph_draft_service.py:1254-1262 (and 417-422, 1236-1251). _limit_notes_to_draft clamps window_end to the 100th note's created_at; the next run sets window_start=that created_at and _staged_notes_in_window uses a strictly-exclusive start (start < created_at <= end). When >=101 staged notes share the exact created_at at the 100-note boundary, notes sorting after the 100th by note_id are excluded from both batches and never drafted. create_batch_graph_draft does not mutate note.status, so the timestamp window is the sole carried state. Reachable via bulk/programmatic import (e.g. datalad/dvc adapters) assigning coarse timestamps. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Use a (created_at, note_id) continuation cursor, or make the window start inclusive with already-drafted note_id de-dup, or push the boundary before the tie group. Add a test with >=101 same-created_at staged notes asserting none are dropped.
close_reason: Added inclusive automatic batch continuation with successful-run note de-duplication and same-timestamp cutoff regression coverage.

title: delete_group_project_memberships retains SELECT-then-DELETE last-owner TOCTOU
description: src/lab_tracker/services/project_service.py:437-463. cq5.6 made the last-owner invariant atomic for delete_project_membership and the group upsert path (lock_project_owner_memberships + re-count in the same unit_of_work), but delete_group_project_memberships still counts owners via an unlocked query and deletes in a separate unit_of_work, taking NO lock. Two concurrent removals (group-delete vs group-delete, or interleaved with the single-project delete) can both pass the owner-count check and leave a project with zero owners; taking no FOR UPDATE lock, it also defeats the hardened single-project path. No DB-level minimum-owner constraint exists. Postgres runtime, per-request sessions. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Re-count owners under repository.lock_project_owner_memberships(project_id) inside the same unit_of_work that performs the deletes; raise ValidationError if any project would drop to zero owners. Add a concurrency test.
close_reason: Re-counts project owners under lock in the same bulk offboard unit of work and adds a concurrent interleaving regression test.

title: decision-context auto-resolution issues one search per accessible project (per-project N+1)
description: src/lab_tracker/decision_context_use_case.py:171-176, 374-389. When no project_id and no anchor resolves scope, _project_ids_with_search_matches loops over every project from list_projects(limit=CONTEXT_LOOKUP_LIMIT=500) and issues reader.search(query, project_id=..., limit=1) per project (each = query_questions+query_notes), up to ~1000 statements on the get_decision_context request path. Violates Epic 4bk no-per-project-N+1. The single scoped-query primitive already exists in decision_context_query.search (project_ids=accessible). Introduced by 4bk.3 (b2e8b24). From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Replace the per-project loop with one bounded scoped query returning DISTINCT accessible project_ids having a question/note match. Add a test asserting O(1) query count for the auto-resolution path.
close_reason: Replaced per-project decision-context auto-resolution searches with one scoped matched-project lookup and test coverage.

title: Investigate SQLite batch migrations deleting child rows during upgrades
description: While testing CQ5.8, a database upgraded from 0022_goals with goal_links survived the repaired 0023 duplicate-slot migration, but upgrading onward to head produced zero goal_links. This points to later SQLite batch_alter_table rebuilds of parent tables such as goals (likely 0030 and/or 0035) cascading child rows when foreign key enforcement is active. Add a focused migration-path regression and guard the affected parent-table batch migrations without broadening CQ5.8.

title: Invitation tokens are multi-use and username case mismatch mints duplicate accounts
description: Invitation HMAC tokens have no consumption record (verify_invitation_token checks only signature + expiry), so one invite link is reusable for its whole TTL (default 168h). register_auth validates the invitee via normalize_email (lowercased) but creates the account via _normalize_username (strip only, NO lowercase) with a case-sensitive uniqueness check, so Bob@Lab.edu and bob@lab.edu both pass the email check yet store as distinct same-role accounts (no ConflictError). Never escalates beyond the granted role; impact is account-table pollution plus a forwardable single-use-intended link.
design: Canonicalize usernames to lowercase so the email check and the uniqueness store agree, and record invite consumption (reject if a user already exists for the invited email).
notes: Relates chv8.
close_reason: Canonicalized usernames and rejected replayed invitations for existing invited emails

title: Bootstrap admin token printed to logs on every boot
description: docker-entrypoint.sh:55 (added by chv8 fe63767) echoes the LAB_TRACKER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_TOKEN value to stderr unconditionally on every boot, not only at generation - the two generation branches deliberately log only the file path. The token gates first-ADMIN self-registration (routes/auth.py:82-90, hmac.compare_digest) while has_users() is False; the value is constant across restarts and persists in log aggregation (Render), going live again on any disk-loss/empty-users reset while already sitting in historical logs.
design: Scope the echo into the generation else-branch and prefer pointing operators at the on-disk file (as the secret-key branch does), preserving the documented Render first-boot UX without re-leaking on every subsequent boot.
notes: Relates security epic zl9 (no existing child covers token-in-logs).
close_reason: Scoped first-admin token echo to initial generation and logged file path on reuse

title: Record export is a GET with a write side effect
description: GET /record-exports/users/{id} (and the group variant) unconditionally writes a RecordExportEvent on every call (record_export_service.py:38-70, export_id=uuid4(), no idempotency key), violating HTTP safe-method semantics - retry, double-click, cache/proxy revalidation, or prefetch each persists another audit row. Worse, the offboarding guard passes on the presence of any export event whose project_ids superset the attributed projects (no recency/intent filter), so an accidental/prefetched GET can silently satisfy the release guard. Requires an authenticated ADMIN (user variant) or group-owner (group variant), so not anonymous, but an admin browser retry/prefetch still triggers all three problems.
design: Make export a POST (it both returns a download and writes an audit row), or split a safe compute-only GET from an explicit recording POST. Ensure no prefetch path can hit the recording variant.
notes: Same class as 99x.5 (GET persisting state) on a different endpoint; net-new.
close_reason: Changed record export endpoints to POST-only and covered GET no-side-effect behavior

title: Portfolio summary groups projects after pagination - groups split across pages, meta.total mismatch
description: portfolio_summary (portfolio.py:67-71, commit sls 5a2bd43) paginates the flat visible-project list first, then groups only the current page. Projects are ordered by created_at (core.py:90), not group_id, so two projects in one group can land on different pages - the group emits as two PortfolioProjectGroupSummary rows with partial project_count each, unreassemblable by the client. Also meta.total counts PROJECTS while data holds GROUP summaries, so total no longer describes the returned collection. Not a leak (scoping applied before grouping; admin short-circuit preserved). The commit test bakes in the mismatch (meta.total==2 for 2 projects collapsing to 1 group).
design: Group BEFORE paginating: build all group summaries from the full visible_projects list, paginate the group list, set total = number of groups; or order projects by group_id so a group never straddles a page boundary and document that total counts projects. Correct the baked-in test assertion.
notes: Distinct from 4bk.7 (a naive SQL pushdown preserves this bug) and aai.8 (which asserts the endpoint is correct today - this refutes that).
close_reason: Grouped portfolio summaries before pagination and corrected group totals

title: Offboarding guard and per-trainee export miss NULL-FK (legacy/local) records
description: After n1x7 switched the per-trainee filters to the attribution FK, the offboarding guard (_attributed_record_project_ids, project_service.py:543-558) and record export (_collect_records, record_export_service.py:104-129) resolve created_by on the FK only. For rows with a NULL FK - local/offline LOCAL_AUTH_USER_ID rows, or legacy non-UUID strings that 0028 leaves NULL - the records are invisible, so the guard returns an empty project set and membership revocation proceeds while the trainee work is stranded (the exact failure h4ag exists to prevent), and the leaver export is incomplete. Cloud path is healed by the 0028 backfill, so the gap is gated to self-hosted/LAN/offline rows (which chv8 explicitly supports).
design: Filter the guard/export record-discovery on the STRING column (created_by == str(user_id)), or OR both predicates (created_by_user_id == :id OR created_by == :id) in the repository query, reserving the FK-only switch for the public referential-trust list filters. Add a regression test with a NULL-FK record whose created_by string equals the trainee UUID, asserting the guard still blocks revocation. Also document FK-only semantics on the public created_by list filters (legacy non-UUID values now silently return zero rows).
notes: Encompasses the public-list-filter and guard-vs-reassign-predicate facets (same NULL-FK root cause). Relates h4ag, n1x7.
close_reason: Recovered NULL-FK legacy/local attribution rows for export and offboarding guards

title: [medium] Make `docker compose up app` work out-of-the-box (auto-generate secret + bootstrap token)

title: Push portfolio summary scoping, pagination, and aggregates into SQL
description: GET /portfolio/summary re-introduces the per-project query-loop and unbounded-payload anti-pattern epic 4bk targets, and does not meet the isj acceptance criterion to bound payload/pagination. Per-project N+1 sources (portfolio.py, now 324 lines): (1) query_projects(limit=None) loads every project then scopes/paginates in Python (portfolio.py:62-70). (2) _latest_activity_at loads ALL rows of nine entity types per project just to compute one max(timestamp) (portfolio.py:169-190). (3) _count_statuses issues one query per status value with a wasted limit=1 row (portfolio.py:152-166). (4) _owners_for_project runs query_project_memberships per project (portfolio.py:201-214). (5) _triage_flags_for_project (added by 80i after this bead) runs four more unbounded per-project loads - query_datasets/analyses/claims/goals (portfolio.py:244-300). That is ~20 repo round-trips per project, ~1000 per default 50-project page. ACCEPTANCE: the SQL pushdown MUST preserve vkcj.2's group-before-paginate fix (portfolio.py:68-70 builds all group summaries from the full visible list, then paginates GROUPS with total=#groups); a naive project-level LIMIT/OFFSET pushdown would reintroduce the vkcj.2 split-groups/meta.total bug.
design: Pass accessible_project_ids as WHERE project_id IN (:ids) (admin None short-circuit = no filter) plus LIMIT/OFFSET and use the SQL COUNT for total. Replace _latest_activity_at row loads with select(func.max(created_at/updated_at)) grouped by project_id over all visible projects (existing (project_id, created_at) indexes make this index-cheap). Replace per-status queries with SELECT status, COUNT(*) GROUP BY project_id, status per entity type (or at minimum limit=0). Collapses the endpoint to a small fixed number of aggregate queries independent of project count and size.
notes: Net-new instance not in the 4bk.1 checklist (portfolio.py landed 2026-06-15, after the 4bk epic 2026-06-12). Blocked by 4bk.8: extract the shared visible-projects prefix first so the pushdown happens in one place. Body reconciled 2026-06-17 - re-anchored line numbers and added the 80i triage-flag and _owners_for_project N+1 loops (portfolio.py grew 167->324 lines via sls/769.1/769.2/80i/vkcj after this bead was filed).
close_reason: Replaced the portfolio summary route's per-project repository loops with a SQL-backed read model that paginates visible project groups in SQL, fetches only projects for the selected groups, and derives counts, owners, activity, and triage flags with grouped aggregate queries while preserving group-before-paginate semantics.

title: Design and implement dry-run record_evidence_bundle MCP tool
description: Authoring one research result through MCP still requires multiple ID-dependent calls across questions, datasets, analyses, claims, visualizations, and optional source notes. Design and implement an additive composite tool that previews and then creates an evidence bundle while preserving Lab Tracker's strict endpoints and provenance boundaries.
design: Add a record_evidence_bundle surface with dry_run defaulting true, explicit idempotency/natural-key behavior, and no silent over-commit. Split provenance by node type: datasets use content-addressed commit manifests from uploaded/resolved artifacts or supplied manifests; repo-derived provenance applies to analyses/code versions through a resolve_code_provenance primitive. Handle locality explicitly: if the MCP client sees a local artifact path but the API server may not, upload or resolve through MCP rather than assuming the server can read the path. Keep strict create endpoints unchanged and route final writes through existing API validation.
acceptance_criteria: A dry run returns a fully reviewable plan including proposed nodes, links, reused records, warnings, and derived provenance values when derivation is possible. Calling with dry_run=false creates or reuses the expected records through existing API paths and returns stable IDs. Re-running with the same idempotency key or natural keys does not create duplicates. Dirty repo state and unreadable/local-only artifacts produce explicit warnings or errors, not fabricated hashes. Tests cover dry-run, commit, idempotent retry, dataset manifest provenance, analysis code provenance, visualization upload/path handling, and backward compatibility of existing MCP create tools. Ruff and relevant backend/MCP tests pass.
close_reason: Added dry-run/idempotent MCP evidence bundle planner and executor through strict API endpoints

title: Make decision-context MCP output a write-friendly front door
description: lab_tracker_get_decision_context is the intended pre-decision entry point, but its MCP description is generic and task_kind is exposed as a plain string. Improve the tool contract so agents know to call it before read-then-write research tasks and can reuse returned project/entity IDs without extra list calls.
design: Keep the tool read-only. Preserve existing research task_kind values such as plot, analysis, slides, experiment_plan, summary, and research_writing; do not mix them with workflow intents like log_result unless a separate workflow_intent field is introduced. Echo resolved project scope, anchors, candidate IDs, allowed task kinds, and concise guidance for subsequent creates. Coordinate with the schema metadata bead so vocabulary is defined once.
acceptance_criteria: The MCP tool description clearly says to call decision context first for research-facing read-then-write tasks. Responses include enough stable IDs and candidate entities to support subsequent create calls without avoidable project/question/dataset lookups. Existing API response shape stays backward-compatible or changes are additive. Tests cover allowed task_kind reporting and ID echo behavior. Ruff and relevant decision-context/MCP tests pass.
close_reason: Added write-front-door decision-context metadata and MCP call-first guidance

title: Expose MCP schema metadata and enum affordances
description: MCP tools currently expose many controlled values as unconstrained strings, so agents have to infer task_kind, question_type, statuses, goal relations, and link statuses from prose or failed calls. Add a discoverable schema/metadata surface and improve MCP tool schemas/descriptions so agents can see allowed values and status lifecycles at the point of use.
design: Generate schema metadata from the existing source of truth: Pydantic request models, lab_tracker.models enums, decision_context_constants.TASK_KIND_VALUES, and service status-transition maps. Treat viz_type separately as a free-string convention unless a later product decision makes it an enum. Prefer a lab_tracker_describe_schema MCP/API surface plus tighter FastMCP argument metadata where feasible.
acceptance_criteria: Agents can discover allowed task_kind values, entity statuses, question/session/goal enums, goal relation/link-status values, required fields, and known lifecycle transitions without reading source. The generated metadata is tested against model constants so it cannot drift silently. Existing create/list tools remain backward-compatible. Ruff and relevant MCP tests pass.
close_reason: Added source-derived schema metadata discovery via API and MCP, with enum/lifecycle tests

title: MCP agent write ergonomics for Lab Tracker
description: Track additive MCP improvements from the 2026-06-12 Lab-Tracker MCP Agent Ergonomics Proposal rev 2. Goal: make agents reach Lab Tracker for research-context writes by default while preserving retained-v1 schema, API validation, human-gated graph changes, and manifest/code provenance boundaries.
design: Sequence low-risk schema and tool-description changes before composite authoring. Do not overload sessions; sessions remain acquisition activity. Dataset hashes remain content-addressed manifests. Repo-derived provenance applies only to analyses and code versions. viz_type remains a free string unless a separate product decision standardizes it.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads cover schema/enum discovery, decision-context front-door affordances, and a dry-run/idempotent record_evidence_bundle design. Existing strict create endpoints remain backward-compatible. Retained v1 boundaries are unchanged.
close_reason: Completed schema discovery, decision-context front door, and dry-run evidence bundle MCP ergonomics slices

title: Planned-figure specs: promote goal figure_slot from string to structured FigureSpec with origin provenance
description: Goals can be specified before their data/analysis exist — a PI sketches 'plot firing rate vs contrast as Figure 3' on a whiteboard during a lab meeting, months before the recording session or analysis. Today a paper goal's planned figures are bare strings (PaperAttributes.figure_slots: list[str] in goals_attributes.py) and a CANDIDATE_FIGURE GoalLink can only target an already-rendered Visualization entity (which requires analysis_id + file_path). So two things go unrecorded: (1) the INTENT of a planned figure — what is meant to be plotted, against what, to answer which question/claim; and (2) the MECHANISM of its specification — which note/session/whiteboard-asset it originated from, when, and via what medium. This promotes the planned-figure slot from a string to a structured, machine-readable FigureSpec carrying intent + origin provenance, WITHOUT inventing a new entity or table. Follow-on to lab-tracker-co0 (closed).
design: Add a FigureSpec Pydantic model in goals_attributes.py (extra='forbid') and change PaperAttributes.figure_slots from list[str] to list[FigureSpec]. FigureSpec fields: slot (str, required label e.g. 'Figure 3'); intent — x (str|None), y (str|None), grouping (str|None), plot_kind (str|None e.g. scatter/line/bar), comparison (str|None free-text 'this against that'); semantic edges — target_question_id (UUID|None), target_claim_id (UUID|None); origin provenance — origin (EntityRef|None pointing at the note/session/whiteboard-asset), specified_at (date|None), medium (str|None e.g. 'whiteboard','lab_meeting'). Lives in the validated attributes JSON blob — NO schema migration, NO new table. Realization path stays complementary, not duplicated: when a real Visualization is later created, a CANDIDATE_FIGURE GoalLink with slot == FigureSpec.slot links it and candidate->committed marks the slot filled; FigureSpec describes the PLAN, GoalLink records FULFILLMENT. Backward compat: accept legacy list[str] on read and coerce each string s to FigureSpec(slot=s); stored-JSON migration is lazy (on next write). Wire through goals_attributes validation, schemas.py goal create/update payloads, the MCP write tool (suggest_new_goal / update_goal already exist), and the IMAGE_ONLY graph-draft path so a whiteboard photo -> Note.raw_asset -> suggested goal can auto-populate FigureSpec.origin. Boundary: this is the LIGHTWEIGHT option chosen over a first-class PlannedVisualization entity precisely to avoid scope creep — it must stay a thin semantic-metadata layer and NOT become a slot-coverage board, figure-layout editor, or plotting tool (docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md).
acceptance_criteria: A paper goal stores figure_slots as structured FigureSpec objects (x/y/plot_kind/comparison + target_question_id/target_claim_id + origin EntityRef), validated with extra='forbid'. Legacy list[str] figure_slots still validate and round-trip (coerced to FigureSpec(slot=s)). A FigureSpec can be created with an origin note/session BEFORE any Visualization or Analysis exists. Invalid/unknown fields are rejected. Tests in tests/test_goals.py cover: structured create, legacy-string coercion, invalid-field rejection, and origin EntityRef round-trip. No new table or migration; change confined to the attributes blob. Stays within the build-vs-buy boundary (documented).
notes: Existing hooks to reuse: GraphDraftMode.IMAGE_ONLY, GraphDraftSemanticType.SUGGEST_NEW_GOAL / LINK_NODE_TO_GOAL, Note.raw_asset (whiteboard photo), GoalRelation.CANDIDATE_FIGURE, GoalLink.slot, GoalLinkStatus.candidate/committed. Heavier alternative (deferred): a first-class PlannedVisualization entity that CANDIDATE_FIGURE can target before any Analysis exists and that is later realized into a Visualization — revisit only if repeated need proves it.

title: Goals direct CRUD: REST routes + MCP tools
description:

title: Goal attributes registry + per-type validation
description:
Make the flexible JSON 'attributes' blob safe and type-aware without per-type tables.

What to do:
- New src/lab_tracker/goals_attributes.py: a Pydantic model per goal type (PaperAttributes, GrantAttributes, TalkAttributes) all with model_config extra='forbid' so unknown/typo keys are rejected, plus OtherAttributes with extra='allow' as the escape hatch. GOAL_ATTRIBUTE_MODELS registry keyed by GoalType. validate_goal_attributes(goal_type, raw) -> dict that validates and returns model_dump(mode='json'); the persisted blob is always the normalized dump.
- Every field is a pointer or light metadatum (target_venue, doi, funding_agency, mechanism, rfa_number, specific_aims, budget_total, event_name, abstract_due, etc.) — never an artifact body.
- Wire validate_goal_attributes into the goals service create/update path (and later into the change-spine apply step) so human- and AI-created goals validate identically.

title: Goals/outputs: flexible goal entity + node-tagging on the provenance spine
description:
The PI wants Lab Tracker to represent GOALS (aspirational research outputs: papers, grants, talks) and let existing graph nodes (questions, claims, datasets, analyses, visualizations) be tagged 'in relation to' a goal output (e.g. 'this figure is a candidate for Figure 3 of paper X', 'this claim addresses Aim 2 of grant Y'). The relation is often tentative ('possible'), and goal types are heterogeneous, so the representation must be flexible.

Chosen design (from a multi-approach design review): a first-class project-scoped 'goals' table with a validated JSON 'attributes' blob, plus a polymorphic 'goal_links' tag table modeled on NoteTargetModel and carrying a relation + link_status pair like dataset_question_links. Flexibility comes from a per-goal-type Pydantic registry over the JSON attributes (extra='forbid' per type + an 'other' escape hatch), NOT per-type subtables. Goals are a new EntityType node in the graph; creating a goal is direct CRUD, while tagging a node to a goal rides the human-gated GraphChangeSet spine.

v1 decisions: goal types = paper, grant, talk (+ 'other' escape hatch; thesis_chapter/patent are trivial later additions). goal_links uses a synthetic link_id PK so a node can hold multiple relations/slots per goal.

Build-vs-buy guardrail: stays a thin semantic layer on the PROV-O reasoning spine (pointers + edges + light metadata). It must NOT grow into a manuscript editor / reference manager / grants-management or slot-coverage board; that is the line recorded in docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md.
design: Base approach: json-attrs-entity. Tables: goals (goal_id PK, project_id CASCADE FK, goal_type, title, summary Text, status, target_date Date, external_ref String(1000), attributes sa.JSON, created_by, created_at/updated_at; index on project_id,created_at) and goal_links (link_id String(36) PK, goal_id CASCADE FK, entity_type String(30), entity_id String(36), relation String(40), link_status String(20) default candidate, slot String(120) nullable, created_by, created_at; UNIQUE(goal_id,entity_type,entity_id,relation,slot); index ix_goal_links_entity_lookup on entity_type,entity_id,goal_id mirroring ix_note_targets_entity_lookup; index on goal_id,link_status). Enums: GoalType(paper,grant,talk,other), GoalStatus(planned,in_progress,submitted,accepted,abandoned), GoalRelation(contributes_to,addresses,candidate_figure,supporting_evidence,background,methods), GoalLinkStatus(candidate,committed,dropped). EntityType gains GOAL. JSON columns are plain sa.JSON() per repo convention (no JSONB in this codebase). Single alembic head confirmed = 0021_claim_questions (down_revision for new migration 0022).
notes: Source: design workflow synthesis (5 approaches, 4 adversarial lens-judges). Verified against live code: single alembic head 0021_claim_questions; _CREATE_SCHEMAS/_UPDATE_SCHEMAS/_SEMANTIC_ALLOWED_TARGETS dispatch maps in services/graph_draft_validation.py; LINK_NOTE_TO_* family modeled as (UPDATE, NOTE) so there is no generic link primitive (a goal UPDATE applier branch is required); JSON columns use sa.JSON() not JSONB.
close_reason: Completed flexible goals entity, node tagging, API/MCP, graph/frontend, and graph-draft integration.

title: Guard against multiple Alembic heads + document migration convention
description: Alembic migration filenames use decorative NNNN_ prefixes, but Alembic chains on revision/down_revision strings, not the number. This false linearity let a new migration (claim_questions) get authored off 0010 instead of the true head (0020), creating two heads; it was caught only by a cryptic mid-upgrade CommandError. There is no dedicated guard asserting a single head, and no written convention for adding a migration. The 0016->0017_daily / 0017_device branch+merge(0019) is legitimate and stays; revision IDs are immutable (recorded in deployed alembic_version), so renumbering is out of scope.
design: Add tests/test_migrations.py::test_alembic_single_head asserting len(get_heads())==1 with an actionable message (chain off current head / use alembic merge). Add a concise 'Database migrations' note to CLAUDE.md: numbers are decorative, run alembic heads, set down_revision to the head, reconcile divergence with alembic merge. No file renames, no revision-ID changes.
acceptance_criteria: test_alembic_single_head fails clearly when >1 head exists and passes at a single head; CLAUDE.md documents the convention; uv run python -m pytest tests/test_migrations.py and ruff both pass.
close_reason: Added test_alembic_has_single_head guard (verified it fires on a forked second head and passes at a single head) and documented the migration convention in CLAUDE.md. No revision IDs changed.

title: Add claim→question 'answers' relationship (plain answers_question_ids)
description:
Claims have no direct link to the question they answer. Today a claim joins the question hierarchy only transitively via supporting datasets (dataset_question_*), which is ambiguous when a claim draws on datasets addressing different questions. This blocks the questions-first query 'what does the lab currently claim about question X?' and forces the research-group deck to imply a figure/claim->question relationship its edges cannot encode.

Add a plain claim->question 'answers' link: Claim.answers_question_ids: list[UUID]. Verdict (supports/refutes) is inferred from the claim's own statement/status; no outcome_status on the link (decided over the outcome-bearing variant).

Vertical: domain model + ClaimInput; claim_questions association table (mirror claim_datasets/dataset_question_links); mappers; sqlalchemy repository load/save; alembic 0011; schemas ClaimCreate/Update + response; claim_service validation (question in project); routes/claims; MCP create_claim + mcp_api_client; provenance JSON-LD; project_graph edge (claim_question_answers, label 'answers'); presentation_graphs PROJECT_GRAPH_RELATIONSHIPS; the research-group deck JSON + prose; tests across the stack.
design: Relationship string: claim_question_answers; edge direction claim->question; label 'answers'; emitted from project_graph._add_evidence_edges. Storage: claim_questions(claim_id FK->claims CASCADE, question_id FK->questions). No outcome column. Cardinality: list (a claim may answer multiple questions). Surface: retained-v1 core (questions + evidence-linked claims).
acceptance_criteria: answers_question_ids round-trips model<->DB; create_claim (API + MCP) accepts it; service rejects question ids outside the claim's project; project_graph emits claim->question 'answers' edge in full+evidence views; presentation manifest validates with claim_question_answers and the vocabulary test passes; deck JSON uses the answers edge and slide 16 no longer says a figure 'addresses' a question; uv run pytest -q and ruff clean.
close_reason: Implemented plain claim->question answers link across model, persistence, migration 0021, API/MCP, graph builder, provenance, and the research-group deck; 301 tests pass, ruff clean.

Preserve NWB/BIDS metadata round-tripping and question/claim semantic edges.

Imported datasets still export correct PROV-O nodes and question edges. Relevant adapter/provenance tests and Ruff pass.
