title: Decision/design: PROV-O ingestion seam for external artifacts
description: provenance.py already EXPORTS PROV-O/JSON-LD. The integrate decisions (datasets, analyses, notes/ELN) all depend on a symmetric INGESTION seam: a defined way to import external artifacts (DVC/DataLad manifests, MLflow runs, ELN entries) as PROV entities/activities and attach them to questions and claims. This is the cross-cutting enabler that makes pointer-not-reimplementation real and positions Lab Tracker as the integration layer rather than a competitor to any single tool.
design: Define a small ingestion contract: external artifact -> {type (Entity/Activity), canonical URI, content hash(es), tool-native metadata blob, semantic edges to existing questions/claims/datasets/analyses}. Reuse the existing manifest_metadata/nwb/bids JSON blobs for tool-native metadata. Keep ingestion adapters thin and optional; the seam must not require any one external tool. Mirror the term vocabulary already in provenance.py _context().
acceptance_criteria: An ingestion contract documented and aligned with the existing PROV-O export context. At least one adapter (likely the dataset substrate) implemented against it as proof. Round-trip test: an ingested artifact appears correctly in the PROV-O export with its question/claim edges.
close_reason: Implemented the PROV-O ingestion seam: added ExternalArtifactReference helpers, documented the contract in build-vs-buy/internal boundary docs, materialized external artifacts in dataset PROV-O export, and added a DataLad-style dataset round-trip provenance test.

title: Decision: ELN boundary - integrate/link rather than become a lab notebook
description: NoteModel/NoteTargetModel plus project organization overlap heavily with Electronic Lab Notebooks (eLabFTW, Benchling, RSpace, LabArchives) - the biggest mindshare overlap but the worst conceptual fit, since ELNs are document-centric while Lab Tracker is graph-centric. Decide the boundary: integrate with / link out to an ELN, or deliberately avoid ELN scope creep - but do NOT become an ELN.
design: Apply pointer-not-reimplementation: where a lab already uses an ELN, a note can reference an ELN entry (URI + hash) and Lab Tracker keeps the edges the ELN does not model - which question/claim/dataset the note attaches to (NoteTargetModel). Keep the human-gated note-to-graph draft->commit flow (GraphChangeSet/GraphChangeOperation) in-house as a differentiator. Resist adding rich-document/editor features that pull toward becoming an ELN.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded decision (integrate-with-ELN / link-only / stay-standalone-and-bounded). Explicit list of note features in-scope vs out-of-scope (anti-ELN guardrail) added to retained-v1 surface. If integrating, a target ELN identified and its entry-reference shape defined.
close_reason: Recorded decision in docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md and docs/retained-v1-surface.md: link/integrate external ELN entry references but do not become an ELN; retained note scope stays lightweight and graph-centric; filed lab-tracker-8q6 for ELN entry reference support.

title: Decision: integrate experiment tracking (MLflow/W&B) for analyses
description: AnalysisModel captures method_hash, code_version, environment_hash, executed_by, executed_at, and used datasets (AnalysisDatasetModel) - almost exactly an MLflow/W&B run. Maintaining bespoke run tracking competes with a mature category (MLflow, Weights and Biases, Sacred). Decide whether an Analysis becomes a reference to an external run plus the semantic edges, rather than a reimplementation of run tracking.
design: Apply pointer-not-reimplementation: store an external run reference (e.g. MLflow run id/URI) plus environment/code provenance owned by that tool, and keep in Lab Tracker the edges it does not model: which analysis supports which claim (ClaimAnalysisModel) and which question it serves. environment_hash maps to conda/Docker; code_version maps to a git SHA - prefer letting the tracker own those. Do not rebuild run logging/metrics UI.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded decision (integrate / keep-bespoke) and chosen tracker, validated as current. Mapping from AnalysisModel fields onto the external run model. PROV-O export still emits the analysis Activity with its claim/dataset edges. Follow-up implementation issue(s) filed.
close_reason: Recorded decision in docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md: integrate external experiment tracking via MLflow as the default open-source run reference target and W&B as a supported external reference while Lab Tracker keeps analysis-to-dataset and claim-support semantics; filed lab-tracker-jxb.

title: Decision: integrate an external data-versioning substrate for datasets
description: DatasetModel/DatasetFileModel already capture commit_hash, per-file checksum, and manifest_files plus NWB and BIDS metadata - i.e. bit-level provenance fields - but Lab Tracker has no substrate that produces/stores the bytes. NWB/BIDS signals the neuroscience domain, where DataLad (git-annex) and the DANDI archive are native; DVC and lakeFS are general alternatives. Decide whether dataset bytes + versioning are integrated from an external substrate rather than managed bespoke. Generalizes the earlier idea of a .dvc manifest importer into a pluggable manifest source.
design: Apply pointer-not-reimplementation: an adapter reads an external manifest (.dvc pointer, DataLad dataset, lakeFS commit) into the existing manifest_files/checksum/commit_hash fields, and Lab Tracker keeps the question/claim edges the substrate does not model. Make it an OPTIONAL adapter (one of several manifest sources), not a required dependency - labs that just drop files on a share must still work. Couples one ingestion path to the substrate's file format and only helps labs already using it.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded decision and chosen substrate(s), validated as current. Adapter is optional with a clean no-substrate fallback. Follow-up implementation issue(s) filed (e.g. .dvc/DataLad manifest importer). NWB/BIDS metadata round-trips into the manifest.
close_reason: Recorded decision in docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md: integrate dataset versioning through optional DataLad/DANDI, DVC, and lakeFS-style manifest adapters while keeping no-substrate/manual manifests as fallback; filed lab-tracker-97x for the DataLad/DVC adapter.

title: Decision: offload auth/RBAC instead of maintaining bespoke identity
description: Entities UserModel, ProjectMembershipModel, DeviceTokenModel, DeviceEnrollmentModel implement identity, project RBAC, and device enrollment in-house. Device enrollment + token is effectively the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628), a fully standardized flow. Maintaining bespoke auth is high-risk and off-core. Candidates: FastAPI-Users (library altitude, likely sweet spot for single-lab deploys), or an IdP such as Keycloak/Authentik (self-host) or Clerk/Auth0 (SaaS) if multi-tenant. Decide whether to offload and at what altitude (library vs service).
design: Apply pointer-not-reimplementation: Lab Tracker keeps project membership/role edges (which user has which role on which project) in the graph, but delegates credential storage, session/token issuance, and the device grant to the chosen provider/library. Avoid running a full IdP unless multi-tenant requirements justify the operational weight.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded decision (offload-to-library / offload-to-IdP / keep-bespoke-with-rationale). If offloading: a migration sketch for existing UserModel/DeviceToken data and a mapping of project roles onto the provider. Operational cost noted for single-lab installs.
close_reason: Recorded decision in docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md: keep bespoke retained-v1 auth for now, retain Lab Tracker project membership/role edges, and prepare to offload credential/session/device-grant plumbing later; official auth landscape was validated before recording.

title: Split remaining SQLAlchemy mappers by aggregate
description: Follow up on the representation decision and Project mapper pilot from lab-tracker-0if.5. Move the remaining hand-written SQLAlchemy mapper groups out of the monolithic sqlalchemy_mappers.py module into focused aggregate/entity mapper modules while preserving the existing compatibility import surface until callers have migrated.
design: Extract mapper groups incrementally by aggregate, using shared mapper helpers where useful. Repository parts should import focused mapper modules directly; sqlalchemy_mappers.py should remain a compatibility barrel during the migration. Keep behavior unchanged and add/adjust narrow mapper tests for each extracted group.
acceptance_criteria: Question, dataset, note, session, analysis, claim, visualization, graph draft, and membership mapper groups are either extracted into focused modules or intentionally left with written rationale. Existing sqlalchemy_mappers imports continue to work during the transition. Mapper, repository, backend tests, and Ruff pass.

title: Audit and tighten project-scoped write authorization
description: Follow up on the behavior-preserving ProjectAuthorizationPolicy extraction from lab-tracker-0if.8. Audit project-scoped write methods that still rely on global WRITE_ROLES only, including question, dataset, session, analysis, claim, and visualization workflows. Decide and implement least-privilege contributor/owner requirements per workflow without hiding behavior changes inside the policy-refactor bead.
acceptance_criteria: Each project-scoped write workflow has an explicit authorization rule documented in code or tests. Contributor/owner/admin requirements are enforced consistently where chosen. Existing retained-v1 behavior changes are intentional and covered by route/service regression tests. Backend tests and Ruff pass.

title: Split decision context assembly into focused modules
description: Decompose decision_context.py into focused modules. The current decision-context assembly is large enough to obscure separate responsibilities such as querying graph data, selecting relevant records, compacting payloads, and shaping the MCP decision-context response.
design: Split the implementation into focused builders/query/use-case modules while preserving lab_tracker_get_decision_context behavior. Keep the MCP/API-facing response shape stable, and extract pure or easily unit-tested pieces first so representative context packets can be regression-tested.
acceptance_criteria: Representative decision-context outputs remain stable for retained-v1 use cases. Querying, selection, compacting/building, and orchestration responsibilities are separated into focused modules or classes. Focused unit tests cover the extracted parts and existing decision-context/MCP tests pass.
close_reason: Split decision-context assembly into focused query, selection, builder, and use-case modules with regression coverage.

title: Make visualization assets portable across workstations
description: Some visualization records point at machine-local paths such as /Users/samuelbrudner/... rather than managed/downloadable assets. This made the coworker overview deck rely on available local plot PNGs instead of PhD visualization record files. Move or upload key visualization files into managed storage, expose stable download paths, and update records/docs so graph consumers can render them on any workstation.
acceptance_criteria: Visualization records needed for demos use managed assets or stable portable paths; API/UI can download or render them from another workstation; docs describe how to attach portable visualization assets.

title: Create coworker overview presentation
description: Build a bare-bones PowerPoint overview of the Lab Tracker repo, including useful visuals and real graph outputs from the app/live records.
acceptance_criteria: Deck explains what the repo does, includes actual project graph visuals or graph exports, includes live record/evidence visuals, and final PPTX is rendered/verified.
close_reason: Created and verified coworker overview PPTX

title: Add lab_tracker init consumer scaffolder
description:
Add an lt setup or lab_tracker init command that scaffolds Lab Tracker integration files into any consumer repository in one step.

The LiteratureEmbeddings setup required hand-written scripts/lt.py, .mcp.json, AGENTS.md Lab Tracker guidance, and lt_ids-style state. New consumers should start with those files generated from Lab Tracker-owned templates.
design:
Implement a console entrypoint, e.g. lab_tracker init [--target REPO_PATH] [--project-name ...]. Generate .mcp.json using the portable MCP launch path, scripts/lt.py as a thin re-export from lab_tracker_client, AGENTS.lt.md or an AGENTS.md fragment documenting the three-mechanism decision tree, and lt_ids.json as a placeholder or project-name-driven bootstrap output.

Keep scaffolding idempotent: do not overwrite local changes without an explicit force flag, and report created/skipped files. The AGENTS fragment should distinguish MCP for lightweight reads, script/client upserts for substantive notes, and CLI for terminal scratch work, and it should document the canonical first-line-marker idempotency pattern.
acceptance_criteria: mkdir new-project; cd new-project; lab_tracker init produces a repo state with portable .mcp.json, scripts/lt.py, AGENTS.lt.md or AGENTS fragment, and lt_ids.json. python -m scripts.lt health succeeds when Lab Tracker is reachable and configured. Generated files use lab_tracker_client and portable lt-mcp/LAB_TRACKER_PYTHON wiring rather than absolute local paths. The command is idempotent and has tests for create, already-exists, and force/overwrite behavior. Backend tests and ruff pass.
close_reason: Implemented lab_tracker init scaffolder plus generated scripts/lt.py shim, portable .mcp.json, AGENTS.lt.md fragment, lt_ids.json placeholder, lab_tracker/lab-tracker console entry points, and lt/lab_tracker_client CLI support. Gates: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q (259 passed) and .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m ruff check . passed.

title: Centralize project authorization checks
description: Centralize project-scoped authorization instead of sprinkling role, project lookup, and contributor checks across service methods. The current pattern relies on each method remembering the right preamble.
design: Introduce a policy object as the default approach, because project-scoped role logic is domain behavior and often needs explicit inputs and results. Services should depend on the policy and call named policy methods for read/write/review actions. Avoid decorator-only enforcement as the primary abstraction.
acceptance_criteria: Representative project read/write/review checks go through one policy surface. Services no longer open-code the common role/project/contributor preamble where the policy applies. Regression tests cover allowed and denied access for representative workflows, including leakage prevention.
close_reason: Centralized project authorization in ProjectAuthorizationPolicy, wired it through LabTrackerAPI, ProjectService, NoteService, and GraphDraftService while preserving existing behavior. Added policy and composition tests; filed follow-up lab-tracker-sbo for least-privilege write tightening. Gates: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_project_authorization_policy.py tests/test_project_collaboration.py tests/test_project_graph_routes.py -q (11 passed), .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q (271 passed), .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m ruff check . (passed).

title: Move request validation into Pydantic schemas where practical
description: Move service-level request validation into Pydantic create/update schemas where practical. Validation such as non-empty fields, metadata normalization, file-list normalization, and claim confidence currently lives partly in services and partly in schemas, making the trust boundary fuzzy.
design: Use Pydantic v2 field validators/model validators on request schemas where the rule belongs to input validation. Keep service-level checks for rules that require repository lookups, permissions, status transitions, or cross-entity invariants. If this touches shared helper cleanup together with status transition work, coordinate with that bead.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid request payloads fail at the schema boundary where applicable. Service methods no longer duplicate schema-only validation. Existing invalid-payload tests pass or are updated to assert schema-level errors. Backend tests pass.
close_reason: Moved practical request-shape validation into Pydantic schemas: nonblank string validators, duplicate UUID-list checks, and note metadata normalization. Regenerated the Lab Tracker skill API reference. Service guardrails remain for direct API and repository/domain-context checks. Gates: schema/reference focused tests (6 passed), full pytest (295 passed), Ruff (passed).

title: Genericize status transition validation
description: Replace duplicated status-transition helper functions with a generic transition validator. Question, dataset, session, analysis, and claim status checks currently repeat the same shape with different enum tables.
design: Introduce a generic helper that accepts the current enum value, next enum value, and transition table. Preserve current allowed transitions and error wording unless a test intentionally updates the wording.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicated status-transition functions are removed or reduced to thin wrappers. Question, dataset, session, analysis, and claim transition behavior is unchanged. Relevant transition tests pass.
close_reason: Reduced duplicated status transition helpers to thin wrappers over a generic transition validator while preserving current error messages and behavior. Gates: focused transition/service tests (16 passed), full pytest (291 passed), Ruff (passed).

title: Decide whether the three-representation model layer is earning its keep
description: Make an explicit design decision for whether Lab Tracker should keep paying the cost of separate domain models, SQLAlchemy ORM models, Pydantic schemas, and hand-written mappers. The current architecture is clean, but the three-representation model creates a large maintenance multiplier and the mapper layer must be updated manually for each field.
design: Evaluate the full representation strategy, not just mapper boilerplate: keep separate domain/ORM/schema layers, collapse domain and ORM with SQLAlchemy 2.0 typed models plus Pydantic from_attributes, adopt SQLModel, derive schemas from domain/ORM models, or generate mapper boilerplate. Record the chosen path and rationale in the bead before broad implementation. Use one pilot entity to prove persistence behavior, validation/wire behavior, migration cost, and test strategy before spawning broader implementation beads.
acceptance_criteria: The bead records a concrete written direction for domain models, ORM models, Pydantic schemas, and mapper responsibilities, including why the chosen tradeoff is worth it for retained-v1. One pilot entity demonstrates the chosen approach without regressing persistence or API behavior. Follow-up implementation beads are created for wider migration or cleanup if needed. Backend tests relevant to the pilot pass.
notes:
2026-05-28 representation decision for retained-v1:

Keep the three explicit representations for now. Domain models remain the service/repository contract and the place where retained-v1 domain fields are expressed without SQLAlchemy session behavior leaking upward. SQLAlchemy ORM models remain persistence-only database rows. Pydantic schemas remain the HTTP/MCP wire/input boundary rather than being generated from ORM models during retained-v1.

Do not collapse to SQLAlchemy-as-domain, SQLModel, or generated schemas in this phase. Those options could delete code, but they would also couple route payload shape, persistence mapping, and migration details during an active architecture cleanup. The safer tradeoff is to keep the boundary and reduce its maintenance cost.

Mapper responsibility stays explicit but should move from one monolithic sqlalchemy_mappers.py file into focused aggregate/entity modules with narrow tests and a compatibility barrel for existing imports. The pilot entity is Project: extract Project mapping into a focused mapper module, wire repository persistence through it, preserve the old import surface, and cover mapper plus project persistence/API behavior. Follow-up work should split the remaining mapper groups in the same style.
close_reason: Recorded retained-v1 representation decision to keep domain/ORM/schema boundaries, extracted Project mapper as the pilot with compatibility re-exports, wired project repository to the focused mapper, and filed follow-up lab-tracker-0la for remaining mapper groups. Gates: tests/test_sqlalchemy_mappers.py and project repository CRUD (7 passed), project HTTP CRUD route (1 passed), full pytest (281 passed), Ruff (passed).

title: Split MCP server into client, tool modules, and registration entrypoint
description: Split the large MCP server module into the API HTTP client, grouped MCP tool modules, and a small registration/entrypoint layer. The current file combines auth retry client behavior, many MCP tool definitions, schema helpers, and module startup.
design: Create a client module for HTTP/auth/retry behavior, grouped tool modules by aggregate or workflow, and a server/entrypoint module that registers tools. Preserve the API-backed boundary: MCP tools call the Lab Tracker API and do not write directly to the database.
acceptance_criteria: python -m lab_tracker.mcp_server still starts the MCP server. Existing MCP tests pass. Tool payload and response behavior is unchanged. No direct DB writes are introduced.
close_reason: Split MCP server into API client, grouped tool modules, resource registration, and a thin entrypoint while preserving tool behavior.

title: Split graph draft service into context builder, validator, applier, and orchestrator
description: Break up the large graph draft service module into focused, testable components. The current service mixes workflow orchestration, context-packet construction, model patch validation, patch application, and permission checks in one large module.
design: Extract GraphContextBuilder, GraphPatchValidator, GraphPatchApplier, and a smaller GraphDraftService orchestrator. Prefer pure functions/classes for context building and validation. Avoid broad constructor rewiring until the service-composition direction is stable; low-risk pure extraction can start earlier.
acceptance_criteria: Graph draft behavior is unchanged for retained-v1 note-scoped review. Builder, validator, and applier responsibilities are separated and covered with focused unit tests. Existing graph draft integration tests pass.
close_reason: Split graph draft context building, patch validation, and patch application into focused components with regression coverage.

title: Clarify project graph visual encoding
description: Add visual cues to the project graph explorer so the left-to-right layout and node color scheme are self-explanatory.
close_reason: Added graph flow axis labels, color swatch legend, tests, and rebuilt frontend bundle.

title: Audit capture composer button types
description: Audit mobile capture composer buttons and similar frontend button patterns for hidden no-op or accidental-submit behavior. An initial text-regex pass flagged composer buttons, but a parser-backed JSX audit showed those controls already declare type=button.
design: Scope to the capture form. Do not change intended submit buttons elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: Parser-backed audit reports no onClick buttons inside forms missing type=button, no actionless buttons outside forms, and no submit buttons outside forms. No code change is required for this audit bead.
close_reason: Closed after parser-backed button audit: the initial regex finding was a false positive caused by JSX arrow syntax; the capture composer buttons already declare type=button and no code change is needed.

title: Add project graph visualization utilities
description: Implement read-only project graph APIs, Mermaid export, and an in-app React Flow explorer with Evidence, Questions, and Full Graph views.
acceptance_criteria: GET /projects/{project_id}/graph and /graph/mermaid return deterministic project graph views; /app/graph renders React Flow tabs with node navigation and Mermaid current-view export; backend and frontend tests cover graph views, escaping, routing, tab behavior, and export.
close_reason: Implemented project graph APIs, Mermaid export, and React Flow explorer.

title: Add MCP evidence authoring tools
description: Expose first-class API-backed MCP creation tools for targeted notes, datasets, analyses, claims, and visualizations. Keep commit_analysis deferred; update skill/docs and tests for the end-to-end evidence authoring flow.
acceptance_criteria: MCP registers create_dataset/create_analysis/create_claim/create_visualization and create_note accepts targets. Client methods call existing API routes with schema-compatible JSON. Tests cover payloads, successful evidence graph creation, and validation failures. Skill/docs describe evidence authoring order and retrospective conventions.
close_reason: Implemented MCP evidence authoring tools, docs, and tests.

title: Preserve uploaded source-file metadata for graph drafting
description: Uploaded photos, audio, and files that enter the staged preproposal review path need source-file metadata so AI graph draft proposals can reason about when and how the artifact was captured. Add upload-time metadata for filename, MIME type, size, checksum, storage timestamp, and client-supplied created/last-modified timestamps; make mobile capture send browser file timestamps when available; ensure graph-draft context carries the metadata.
design: Keep note.metadata scalar-only. Use prefixed source_file_* keys to avoid colliding with user metadata. Treat client created/last-modified timestamps as optional provenance, and use storage timestamp as ingestion provenance.
acceptance_criteria:
- /notes/upload-file persists normalized source-file metadata alongside user metadata
- /notes/quick-capture stages file metadata instead of dropping all metadata
- Mobile capture includes File.lastModified-derived metadata for photo and audio uploads, including offline queued uploads
- Graph draft context/source artifacts expose the uploaded metadata for proposal generation
- Tests cover full upload, quick capture, and graph-draft context metadata
close_reason: Source-file metadata is added to full uploads and quick capture, mobile capture sends browser file timestamps, graph-draft context carries the enriched metadata, and backend/frontend tests cover the behavior.

title: One-tap phone pairing: QR + auto-submit + reachable URLs
description:
The pairing flow shipped under lab-tracker-bbd works but has three manual steps that defeat the 'no friction' goal: the enrollment URL contains the laptop's origin (often 127.0.0.1, not phone-reachable), there's no QR code so the user has to ferry the URL manually, and the phone shows a label form before pairing.

This bead replaces all three with: server renders a phone-reachable enrollment URL (resolved from request.base_url, overridable via LAB_TRACKER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL); the enrollment response includes an inline-SVG QR code of that URL; the DevicesPage shows the QR prominently next to the copy-URL fallback; the EnrollPage auto-submits with a User-Agent-derived label as soon as it loads, so scanning the QR ends in 'paired and in capture' with one tap.
design: Use segno for QR rendering (pure-Python, SVG-native, no Pillow dep). Determine base URL preference order: explicit setting, then request.base_url, then a hostname warning. EnrollPage keeps a manual override path (?label=foo) so the user can pair multiple phones distinguishably if needed, but defaults to UA-derived label.
acceptance_criteria:
- /auth/devices/enrollment returns enrollment_url that points to the request's external host, not 127.0.0.1
- LAB_TRACKER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL setting overrides the derived host (for tunnels, prod)
- Response includes enrollment_qr_svg containing valid SVG QR encoding the enrollment URL
- DevicesPage renders the QR inline; copy-URL is the fallback
- EnrollPage auto-submits on load, no label form required, label sourced from User-Agent
- End-to-end smoke: scan QR on iPhone Camera, tap pop-up, lands at /app/capture as paired device with no further taps
close_reason: Closed

title: Batch draft service: persist proposals + retry/dead-letter
description:
Service-level orchestration that ties together build_batch_graph_context (lab-tracker-jdy) and the pluggable draft_from_batch client (lab-tracker-641). Given a set of staged notes, it builds the context packet, calls the configured client, persists the resulting proposal set as a pending batch with full traceability back to the source notes, and handles model failures with bounded retries + a dead-letter record so the runner can surface them.

Splits out of lab-tracker-641 once the provider abstraction and the OpenAI client method landed; persistence touches the data model (GraphChangeSet currently ties to a single source note and needs either schema extension or a sibling BatchGraphDraft entity) and warrants its own commit and review pass.
design: Decide: extend GraphChangeSet to carry a list of source_note_ids, or introduce BatchGraphDraft wrapping multiple GraphChangeSets/change-set-equivalents. Either way, every operation in the persisted record must trace back to the note(s) that motivated it via existing source_refs. Retries: bounded (e.g. 3) with exponential backoff for transient HTTP errors; non-retryable validation failures go straight to dead-letter. Dead-letter is a persisted record with the failure category, error text, and the offending input so a human can inspect.
acceptance_criteria:
- create_batch_graph_draft(notes, *, user_hint=None, actor=None) on the service layer
- Persists a pending batch with operation-level traceability to source note ids
- Retries transient model errors with bounded attempts + backoff
- Dead-letter record on terminal failure with category, error, and input snapshot
- Tests cover: success path persistence, retry on transient error, dead-letter on terminal error, empty-batch short-circuit
close_reason: Implemented batch graph-draft persistence with source-note traceability, bounded retries, validation/model dead-letter metadata, and coverage for success, retry, dead-letter, and empty windows. Gates: pytest 320 passed; ruff passed; frontend test/lint/build passed.

title: Implement decision-context MCP tooling for assistant clients
description: Implement the product spec in docs/mcp-decision-context-tooling.md: add a read-only decision-context API/MCP tool, expose retained-v1 low-level read tools for datasets/analyses/claims/visualizations and provenance, add consultation policy resource, update AGENTS/skill instructions, and test task-kind validation, graph context retrieval, truncation, ambiguity, and read-only behavior.
close_reason: Implemented API-backed decision context endpoint, MCP integration, low-level read tools, policy resource/docs, and validation tests.

title: Specify decision-context MCP tooling for assistant clients
description: Write product specs for new Lab Tracker MCP tooling that lets Codex and other assistants consult the backend knowledge graph before choosing plots, analyses, slides, research writing structure, or other research-facing work. The spec should define trigger policy, task kinds, read-only context APIs, response schema, integration with AGENTS/skills, acceptance criteria, and non-goals.
close_reason: Product spec written in docs/mcp-decision-context-tooling.md and linked from docs/lab-tracker-mcp-skills.md. Follow-up implementation bead lab-tracker-dp4 created.

title: Batch review UI: approve/reject proposal sets
description:
Extend the existing graph-draft review card pattern (referenced in commit 502390c) to a batch container. The user sees a pending batch as a single review session: one report summarizing all proposed changes, with per-item accept / reject / edit, plus 'approve all' / 'reject all' shortcuts. Tabs (per proposed change, or per change category) are an acceptable way to organize the report if a single scroll gets unwieldy.

Approved operations commit through the existing graph mutation path. Rejected and edited operations are recorded for future model feedback so the system improves over time.
design: Desktop-first (decision 2026-06-10): review is expected to happen at a computer. Do not constrain layout or markup for phone rendering — mobile is fine if it falls out for free, but it is never a design constraint. The batch report is one document covering all proposed changes in the batch; tabbed navigation between proposed changes is an optional organizing device, not a requirement.
acceptance_criteria:
- /app/batches lists pending batches with timestamp, note count, op count
- Detail view is a single report summarizing the whole batch; each proposed op has accept/reject/edit controls (tabs per change optional)
- Approved ops commit via existing graph mutation API
- Rejected/edited ops persist with reason metadata for model feedback
- Empty state when no pending batches
- No mobile-layout requirement: desktop review is the target
close_reason: Implemented /app/batches queue, batch detail review via existing graph-draft card, per-operation accept/reject/edit with decision notes, empty state, and desktop-first batch review flow. Gates: pytest 320 passed; frontend test/lint/build passed.

title: Batch draft generator: configurable provider + OpenAI batch client
description:
Given a batch context packet (from the context builder), call Claude to produce a structured set of proposed graph operations: new nodes, new edges, claim updates, suggested links between notes and existing graph entities, and proposed multi-note merges (e.g. three gel photos -> one observation).

Output is a structured JSON proposal stored as a 'pending batch' record for the review UI. No commits happen ? only proposals.
acceptance_criteria:
- Given a context packet, returns a structured proposal set (typed schema)
- Supports multi-note merge proposals
- Supports link proposals (note -> question/session/dataset)
- Stores result as a pending batch with full traceability back to source notes
- Failure modes (model timeout, invalid JSON) handled with retries + dead-letter
notes: Closed with the provider abstraction (GraphDraftClient Protocol + make_graph_draft_client factory) and the OpenAIGraphDraftClient.draft_from_batch method landed in commit 1872618. Settings gain graph_draft_provider (default openai). Persistence of batch proposals as pending review records, plus retry/dead-letter handling, are split out into lab-tracker-8ay because they touch the data model and warrant a separate commit. Provider clients for Claude and Gemini are tracked as lab-tracker-dvt and lab-tracker-z66.
close_reason: Closed

title: Batch context builder: assemble notes + graph slice for the model
description:
Build the context packet the model sees when drafting a daily batch. Should include: the full set of unprocessed notes (text, transcripts, image references), the relevant slice of the graph (projects/questions/sessions touched by those notes, plus their immediate neighbors), and any prior batch decisions on related entities.

This is what differentiates the daily batch from per-note drafting ? the model can see multiple related notes together and propose merges/relationships it couldn't see one at a time.
acceptance_criteria:
- Given a set of staged notes, returns a context packet with: notes payload, relevant graph subgraph, recent related decisions
- Context size bounded (paginated or truncated with priority signals if oversized)
- Tested with synthetic batches of varying size and graph density
- Output schema documented so the draft generator can consume it
close_reason: Closed

title: Batch runner: agent scheduled at user-set cadence, idempotent draft job
description:
Add a scheduled job driven by a user-facing cadence setting (default daily, e.g. 06:00 local lab time — not hard-coded). Setting or changing the cadence (re)schedules an agent that wakes up at that cadence, collects all notes with status='staged' that arrived since the last successful run, and kicks off the batch context builder + draft generator to figure out proposed graph changes.

Must be idempotent: re-running the same window must not produce duplicate batches. Should record run start/end, window covered, notes included, and outcome (success/error) for observability.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cadence is a user-visible setting (default daily 06:00 local lab time); changing it reschedules the agent/job
- On wake, job collects staged notes since last successful run watermark
- Idempotent: re-running same window does not create duplicate batches
- Run history persisted with window, note count, status, errors
- Manual 'run now' trigger available for admins/dev
close_reason: Implemented user-visible batch cadence settings, due-run listing, idempotent run keys, persisted run history, and manual run-now trigger. Gates: pytest 320 passed; ruff passed; frontend test/lint/build passed.

title: Device-bound auth (passkey or long-lived device token) for phone
description:
Username + password on a phone keyboard is the single worst friction point. After the first desktop login, the user should pair their phone once (QR code from desktop, magic link, or WebAuthn passkey enrollment) and never type a password on the phone again.

Token lives in IndexedDB scoped to the installed PWA. Revocable from a 'My devices' page on desktop. No biometric requirement at this stage ? long-lived bearer token is acceptable for the trust model (single-user lab notebook).
design: Two options to evaluate: (a) WebAuthn passkey ? most secure, supported on modern iOS/Android, requires platform authenticator UX; (b) QR-code pair flow ? desktop generates a short-lived enrollment URL with embedded device-token signing material, phone scans, stores long-lived token. Option (b) is simpler to ship; option (a) is the long-term right answer. Pick one and document the reason.
acceptance_criteria:
- After first pairing, phone capture works without entering credentials
- Device tokens revocable from a desktop 'My devices' view
- Tokens scoped so they can call /notes/quick-capture and the share-target handler, nothing destructive
- Decision recorded for passkey vs. QR pair flow with rationale

title: Epic: Scheduled AI graph-draft batch (user-set cadence)
description:
Replace per-note draft generation with a scheduled batch at a cadence the user sets. Drafting on every upload thrashes context and wastes model calls on incomplete information; a batch cadence lets the model see accumulated notes together, dedupe, propose coherent multi-note merges, and produce a single review queue.

Goal: at the user-set cadence (daily is a sensible default, not a requirement), a scheduled agent wakes up, collects all notes that landed since the last run, builds a graph-aware context packet covering them, tries to figure out proposed graph operations (new nodes, edges, claim updates), and stores the result as a pending batch in the existing graph-draft review UI. The human reviews per batch instead of per note.

Pairs with the 'PWA capture-first phone workflow' epic: capture cheaply through the day, review proposals in one sitting.
design:
Batch is the unit of review, not the individual note. Cadence is a user-facing setting: setting or changing it (re)schedules an agent that wakes up at that cadence, reads the accumulated inputs, and tries to figure out the changes. Runner is idempotent (re-runnable on the same window without duplicates). Context builder pulls unprocessed notes + the relevant graph slice (projects/questions touched). Draft generator can propose merges across multiple notes (e.g. three photos from the same gel become one observation). Review UI extends the existing graph-draft card pattern to a batch container.

Report/review surface decisions (2026-06-10): review is expected to happen at a computer, so do NOT constrain report layout for phones (fine if it happens to render there, but never a design constraint). One report summarizes all proposed changes in a batch; tabs per proposed change (or per change category) are an acceptable way to organize it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Scheduled agent runs at the user-set cadence, idempotently, with configurable window
- Cadence is a user setting; changing it reschedules the agent
- Batch context builder collects all notes since last successful run + relevant graph slice
- Draft generator produces a structured proposal set covering the batch
- A single report/review surface summarizes all proposed changes in the batch (tabs per change optional), with per-operation accept/reject
- Approved operations commit through the existing graph mutation path
- Rejected/edited operations are recorded for future model feedback
- Notification surfaces when a new batch is ready for review
close_reason: Completed scheduled graph-draft batches end-to-end: user-set cadence and due/manual runner, idempotent persisted batch runs, batch proposal persistence with traceability and dead-letter metadata, Anthropic/Google providers, desktop batch review queue/detail with per-operation accept/reject/edit and model-feedback notes, and in-app ready-batch notification. Gates: pytest 320 passed; ruff check src tests scripts alembic skills passed; npm run test:frontend passed; npm run lint:frontend passed; npm run build:frontend passed.

title: Epic: PWA capture-first phone workflow
description:
Make phone note capture nearly effortless. The current /app/capture screen requires login, mandatory project selection, and a network round-trip before anything is saved ? too much friction for one-handed bench work.

Goal: a user takes a photo with their phone's normal Camera app, hits Share, picks Lab Tracker, and the note is staged. No browser open, no login each time, no fields required beyond the captured asset.

This requires turning the existing static-bundle frontend into a Progressive Web App: web app manifest (Add to Home Screen), service worker (offline asset cache + upload retry queue), Web Share Target (OS share-sheet integration), and a device-bound auth path (passkey or long-lived device token) that eliminates the password prompt on phone. The note API also needs a minimal-payload quick-capture endpoint that accepts asset + device-default project and defers all linking to the daily draft review.

Pairs with the 'Daily AI graph-draft batch' epic: capture cheaply now, AI proposes structured graph updates once a day for human review.
design: Phone capture flow target: Camera -> Share Sheet -> Lab Tracker -> staged. <3 taps, works offline. Auth via device-bound passkey/token in IndexedDB, not username/password. Quick-capture endpoint accepts only asset + project; everything else (question/session/dataset links) gets proposed by the daily batch and confirmed in the review card.
acceptance_criteria:
- manifest.json served with icons, theme, start URL
- Service worker caches the app shell and queues failed uploads with retry
- Web Share Target registered so OS share sheet routes photos to a capture endpoint
- POST /notes/quick-capture accepts minimal payload (asset + project_id), returns 202 if queued
- Device-bound auth path lets a phone authenticate without typing a password on each visit
- Offline capture survives a network drop and syncs when connectivity returns

title: Clarify and harden MCP note creation validation for status and metadata
description:
While recording the 2026-04-28 temporal-gradient projector titration analysis through the Lab Tracker MCP connector, `lab_tracker_create_note` accepted only a reduced payload after two confusing validation failures.

Observed behavior:
- Creating a note with `status="active"` failed, while the analogous question flow accepts `active`. This is technically consistent with `NoteStatus` (`staged`, `committed`, `archived`), but the MCP tool exposes `status` as a free string and the skill/API docs do not make the note-specific allowed values obvious.
- Creating a note with structured metadata failed unless all metadata values were strings. `NoteCreate.metadata` is typed as `dict[str, str]`, so Pydantic rejects non-string JSON values before the request reaches `_normalize_note_metadata`, even though the service normalizer is written to coerce non-string values to strings.
- The successful fallback was to create the note with `status="staged"` and no metadata, which avoided data loss but made the assistant workflow more brittle and less informative.

Concrete example context:
- Project: `b97935f1-42c6-475d-b35f-0e23607d11e6`
- Successful fallback note: `4dc2ec50-7781-475d-ba3d-b89c0c79895b`
- MCP tool: `lab_tracker_create_note`
- Relevant code paths noticed during triage: `src/lab_tracker/schemas.py` (`NoteCreate.metadata: dict[str, str]`, `status: NoteStatus | None`), `src/lab_tracker/mcp_server.py` (`lab_tracker_create_note(status: str | None, metadata: dict[str, str] | None)`), and `src/lab_tracker/services/shared.py` (`_normalize_note_metadata` coerces values).

Why this matters:
Assistant clients will naturally use project/question status vocabulary and structured provenance metadata. The current behavior requires hidden knowledge of note-specific status values and silently discourages preserving useful machine-readable provenance on notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- `lab_tracker_create_note` docs/schema expose the allowed note statuses (`staged`, `committed`, `archived`) clearly, or the MCP layer rejects invalid statuses with a targeted error before the generic API failure.
- Decide whether note metadata should accept JSON scalar values and normalize them, or remain string-only; make the API schema, service normalizer, MCP type hints, and docs agree.
- Add or update tests for MCP note creation covering invalid note status and metadata values with at least one non-string scalar.
- Update the Lab Tracker skill/docs so assistant clients know the note status vocabulary and metadata contract.
close_reason: Clarified note status validation and aligned scalar metadata handling across API, MCP, tests, docs, and installed skills.

title: Decision: shipped-vs-deferred prose drift is NOT automatable - use a PR checklist + per-release pass
description: DECISION, not a code guard. The 'shipped feature described as deferred/not-shipping' prose drift (lmc3.2 batch drafting, lmc3.8 offline capture) has NO machine-checkable truth and cannot be reliably automated: a keyword blocklist would inherit the very drift it guards, and the prose authorities already contradict each other (configuration.md:175 calls offline capture deferred while retained-v1-surface.md and the mobile doc call it shipped). Instead: add one line to the PR template / docs-review checklist ('If this PR ships a feature, grep docs for it being called deferred/future and update retained-v1-surface.md'), and do a per-release human pass over the 'Deferred Workflows' list. The route-parity guard (.3) partially backstops this by forcing new shipped surface to be triaged into a category. From drift-guard design 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: PR template / CONTRIBUTING gains the shipped-vs-deferred reminder line, and a per-release docs pass over the deferred-workflows list is documented as the cadence.

title: Clarify decision-context ambiguous match window at high volume
description: Follow-up from the rjg1 verification review. lab-tracker-rjg1.2 replaced per-project searches with one scoped matched-project lookup, but the global 500-row match window can narrow ambiguous-project detection when pathological volumes of matches crowd out another matching project. This does not leak data and still auto-resolves to a real match, but the limit should be documented/tested or the lookup should count distinct matching projects more exactly.
acceptance_criteria: Decision-context project auto-resolution has explicit tested behavior when more than 500 scoped question/note matches exist across projects: either widen/count distinct matching project ids so ambiguity is preserved, or document and test the bounded-window behavior; no cross-project leakage; tests pass.

title: Add real-reader coverage for decision-context matched-project lookup
description: Follow-up from the rjg1 verification review. lab-tracker-rjg1.2 fixed the decision-context per-project N+1, but its O(1) coverage uses a fake reader. The real DecisionContextQueryReader path should be covered for query count, accessible-project scoping, and note-only matches. The old project_ids_from_search helper appears to be dead production code after the fix.

close_reason: Added real RepositoryDecisionContextReader coverage for scoped question/note project matching with bounded query count and removed dead helper.

title: Chunk batched goal-link cleanup target filters for large SQLite deletes
description: Follow-up from the rjg1 verification review. lab-tracker-rjg1.10 collapsed project-delete goal-link cleanup into one query_goals(target_entity_keys=...) call using a composite IN predicate. That removes the N+1, but a very large project delete can still exceed SQLite's bound-parameter limit when target_entity_keys is huge. Postgres runtime is unaffected, but SQLite tests/local use should avoid the too-many-SQL-variables failure path.
acceptance_criteria: query_goals or remove_goal_links_to_project_contents chunks target_entity_keys below SQLite's parameter limit while preserving one-goal de-duplication; add a regression test with enough cascaded target entities to exercise chunking; existing goal/project-delete tests pass.
close_reason: Chunked project-delete goal reverse lookups below SQLite parameter limits and added regression coverage.

title: Service-worker CACHE_VERSION / asset ?v not bumped despite app.js bundle change
description: src/lab_tracker/frontend/sw.js:12-22. This batch rebuilt the committed bundle (app.js content changed, new markers present) but CACHE_VERSION stayed v18 and SHELL_ASSETS still references app.js?v=18 / styles.css?v=18. The SW serves /app/static/* cache-first and only purges non-v18 caches. Self-mitigated THIS cycle because sw.js's own bytes changed (forces reinstall -> cache.addAll), but a future batch changing only app.js while leaving sw.js/?v fixed would serve a stale bundle to installed PWA users. The static-asset test only enforces v-alignment, not a bump-on-bundle-change. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Drive ?v / CACHE_VERSION from a content hash, or bump them whenever the bundle content changes; add a test that fails if the bundle changed without a version bump.
close_reason: Stamped service-worker cache and asset query versions from shipped app.js/styles.css bytes, with a regression test that recomputes the expected hash.

title: Migration 0023 was edited in place to add the cq5.8 dedupe (immutability anti-pattern)
description: src/lab_tracker/alembic/versions/0023_goal_link_slot_not_null.py:14-58. The cq5.8 _dedupe_unslotted_goal_links() was added to upgrade() of an already-deployed, descendant-chained revision (0023, 17 descendants, head=0040) rather than a new forward-only revision - violating the project immutability rule (CLAUDE.md). Databases that already ran pre-edit 0023 never re-execute it. Data risk is near-nil (pre-edit 0023's bare UPDATE...SET slot='' would itself have crashed on a DB holding NULL-slot dupes, so a successful apply proves none existed), so this is hygiene, not corruption. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: If 0023 was never deployed anywhere, leave as-is. If it may have been deployed, move _dedupe_unslotted_goal_links() into a new forward-only revision chained after head 0040.
close_reason: Moved unslotted goal-link dedupe into new forward-only 0041 migration and restored 0023 to slot normalization.

title: Dead SQLite FK PRAGMA guard in migrations 0039/0040 (no-op inside Alembic transaction)
description: src/lab_tracker/alembic/versions/0039_not_null_tightening_0014_0024.py:91-94 and 0040_drop_daily_reviews_align_batch_key.py:57-60. _set_sqlite_foreign_keys issues PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF/ON, but Alembic runs migrations inside context.begin_transaction(), where SQLite ignores the PRAGMA - and FK enforcement is already off during migrations (the FK connect-listener is only registered on the app engine, not the migration/test engine). So the guard is doubly inert dead code that misleads future authors. Tests pass regardless. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Drop the ineffective PRAGMA helper, or if suppression is genuinely required set transactional_ddl=False / issue the PRAGMA outside begin_transaction().
close_reason: Made SQLite migration FK suppression explicit with transactional_ddl=False and documented why batch table rebuilds require it.

title: portfolio_query._uuid_values duplicates common.uuid_values
description: src/lab_tracker/portfolio_query.py:112-113 defines a private _uuid_values identical to sqlalchemy_repository_parts.common.uuid_values (the established helper used by analyses/core/datasets/graph_drafts/sessions/notes). portfolio_query.py:51 already imports from that module. Maintainability only - two copies of the accessible-id sort/normalization can drift. New code this batch. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Import uuid_values from sqlalchemy_repository_parts.common and delete _uuid_values.
close_reason: Reused shared uuid_values helper and removed duplicate portfolio helper.

title: Project delete fans out goal-link cleanup into a per-entity N+1
description: src/lab_tracker/services/goal_link_cleanup.py:30-54, 70-75. remove_goal_links_to_project_contents (called from project_service.delete_project:127 inside the delete unit_of_work) issues 7 unbounded query_*(limit=None) scans then one query_goals per discovered target entity. Deleting a large long-lived project becomes O(entities) DB round-trips in a single transaction and can time out / hold a long lock. Admin-gated delete path (outside Epic 4bk's literal scope) but the same fan-out anti-pattern. From deep review 2026-06-18 completeness sweep.
acceptance_criteria: Collect all target keys first, then resolve affected goals with a single query_goals filtered by (entity_type, entity_id) IN (...) (or a join), rather than one query per target.
close_reason: Resolved project-delete goal cleanup with one multi-target reverse goal lookup and regression coverage.

title: import-folder follows symlinks and imports out-of-tree file bytes
description: src/lab_tracker_client/cli.py:280-292. _discover_import_files uses root.rglob('*') filtered by path.is_file(), which follows symlinks; a symlink under --root pointing outside the tree (e.g. ~/.ssh/id_rsa) passes the filter (relative_to(root) still succeeds lexically) and its resolved bytes are read and uploaded as an evidence note, while the recorded source_uri reflects the in-tree symlink path. Local single-user CLI, so a hardening gap not a remote vuln. duz.1 added no symlink handling. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Skip path.is_symlink() during discovery, or require path.resolve() to stay under root.resolve() before reading. Document that symlinks are not followed.
close_reason: Skipped symlinked files during import-folder discovery, documented the behavior, and added symlink regression coverage.

title: DVC/datalad manifest with a float-formatted size crashes the import adapter
description: src/lab_tracker/provenance_ingestion.py:290-294. _optional_int_value does bare int(value) on the str form of the size field; a JSON float '2048.0' or YAML '2048.0' (isdigit() False) becomes int('2048.0') -> ValueError, aborting the whole dataset_manifest_from_dvc/datalad import. No try/except. DVC normally writes integer sizes so likelihood is low, but a malformed/variant manifest fails the entire import. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Parse defensively: try int(value), fall back to int(float(value)) or None on failure. Add a test with a float-formatted size.
close_reason: Parsed manifest size fields defensively and covered DVC/DataLad float-formatted sizes.

title: Graph-draft context bounded-fetch can omit recently-updated / superseded questions at scale
description: src/lab_tracker/services/graph_draft_context.py:371-405. _question_context fetches ACTIVE and STAGED via query_questions(limit=50, recent_first=True) which orders by created_at DESC, then re-sorts the union by updated_at and keeps the top 50 - so an old-created but recently-updated question (project with >50 of a status) is dropped before the updated_at sort sees it. Separately, superseded context fetches the most-recent 100 SUPERSEDED then filters to those pointing at active context; with >100 superseded a relevant entry can be dropped. Both diverge from the prior unbounded-then-sort behavior; LLM context completeness only, no scoping impact. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Add an updated_at-desc ordering option so the SQL LIMIT selects by the final sort key (or widen the fetch); query superseded questions filtered by superseded_by_question_id IN (active_context_ids) in SQL.
close_reason: Added updated_at question ordering and SQL-filtered superseded alias lookup for graph-draft context, with scale regressions.

title: Tighten remaining ORM/migration NOT NULL drift outside 0014-0024
description: CQ5.7 intentionally tightened the deep-review 0014-0024 drift set. A metadata-vs-migrated-schema comparison also found remaining nullable drift outside that scope, including dataset/note metadata fields, project/group/supervision timestamps, analysis external_artifacts, claim external_citations/edge timestamps, and entity_versions snapshot/created_at. Add a separate tightening migration and regression coverage if these should align with Base.metadata.

title: Document 0030 goal-nullable downgrade one-way semantics
description: alembic/versions/0030_nullable_goal_project.py downgrade() restores goals.project_id to nullable=False unconditionally; once projectless (spanning) goals exist it aborts mid-batch with a NOT NULL violation (reproduced on SQLite; Postgres ALTER SET NOT NULL fails equivalently). No downgrade round-trip test exists. Acceptable under the forward-only/revision-immutability policy, but a surprised operator mid-rollback is avoidable.
design: Document the one-way nature in the migration docstring, or have downgrade() first delete/reassign rows where project_id IS NULL or raise a clear actionable error.
notes: Distinct from cq5.7 (upgrade NOT-NULL drift in 0014-0024).
close_reason: Documented one-way downgrade semantics for nullable projectless goals

title: [larger] Managed lab deployment: invite-by-email, role grants, password reset, ops
description:
Standing up Lab Tracker for a lab today is a sysadmin job no typical wet lab can absorb without engineering/IT: Docker + Postgres + hand-set secrets + Administrator firewall rules + raw-HTTP admin bootstrap + undocumented backups. The lab-manager persona could not complete it.

Build lab-admin onboarding as a product concern rather than an ops burden: invite-by-email, role grants, and password reset in the UI (none exist today), plus making backups/restart/upgrades managed (not the lab manager's responsibility). This is the durable fix for the multi-user deployment barrier and complements the first-run admin UI (lab-tracker-5944) and hosted/managed paths (lab-tracker hosted-demo + desktop/cloud template).

Evidence: audit "lab deployment" dimension; barriers #8, #9, #13; lab-manager-deploy persona.
acceptance_criteria: A non-engineer lab admin can invite members by email, assign roles, and reset passwords from the UI; backups and upgrades are handled by the platform, not by manual ops.
notes: 2026-06-15: First-admin setup, global role grants, password reset UI, Docker first-run secrets, and backup/restore docs landed. Invite-by-email and fully managed backups/upgrades/ops remain outside this repo-only pass, so this larger managed deployment item remains open.
close_reason: Added admin-created email invitation links, invite-token registration, existing role/password admin UI coverage, and a managed Render deployment path with platform database backups and restart/redeploy ops.

title: [larger] Signed desktop app or one-click cloud template so no one touches a terminal
description:
There is no installer artifact (.dmg/.exe/.pkg) and no managed deploy; "getting" the software means cloning a public GitHub repo and building it (audit barriers #1-#4), which the target persona is uneasy with and largely unable to do.

Provide a true zero-terminal install: either a signed/notarized desktop app (e.g. packaging the FastAPI server + PWA behind a native shell) or a one-click cloud deploy template (Render/Fly/Railway button) that provisions Postgres, sets secrets, runs migrations, and yields a URL + first-admin flow. Bench scientists then only ever receive a link + login. Larger effort; depends on the launcher (lab-tracker-7x77) and auto-secret Docker work (lab-tracker-z7h2) as building blocks.

Evidence: audit barriers #1, #2, #3; "Discovery" and "Install" dimensions.
acceptance_criteria: A non-technical lab member can obtain and run Lab Tracker with no terminal — either by installing a signed app or clicking a one-click cloud deploy — and end up with a working instance + login.
notes: 2026-06-15: Added lab-tracker serve plus macOS/Windows double-click launchers and documented Docker/LAN setup. This is not yet a signed/notarized desktop app or one-click cloud deploy template, so the zero-terminal distribution item remains open.
close_reason: Added a Render one-click cloud deploy blueprint with managed Postgres, persistent disk, generated auth secret, first-admin setup, startup migrations, and README/docs deploy button.

title: Clarify portfolio running_analysis_count naming (no RUNNING analysis status exists)
description: PortfolioProjectSummary.running_analysis_count counts AnalysisStatus.STAGED, but AnalysisStatus has no RUNNING member (only STAGED/COMMITTED/ARCHIVED). The count is correct but the wire-contract field name implies a nonexistent status, while the sibling draft_dataset_count correctly aliases STAGED datasets as draft. Either rename to staged_analysis_count for symmetry or document running = staged (not-yet-committed) in the schema. Confirm the chosen name against the isj/80i wording before changing the wire contract since lab-tracker-80i triage will consume this field.
notes: Decide before more consumers bind the field.
close_reason: Renamed portfolio analysis count to staged_analysis_count

title: Fix external artifact commit asymmetry and legacy duplicate handling
description: Re-review L2/L3: legacy metadata-encoded external artifacts can satisfy create-committed but update-commit rejects them; duplicate legacy metadata can strand staged datasets and silently alter commit hashes. Track follow-up after c1u.7 hardening. Details: docs/runs/re-review-2026-06-12.md#L2.
close_reason: Aligned update-commit with create-commit for legacy metadata-encoded external artifacts, deduplicated exact legacy artifact metadata entries for mapper/hash stability, and added regressions for legacy update commits, duplicate legacy hash shape, and mapper backfill. Focused tests, provenance tests, touched Ruff, and full pytest pass.

title: Revisit analysis delete guard for rejected claims
description: Re-review L1: analysis delete guard blocks REJECTED claims too, which can make terminal/uneditable analyses permanently undeletable. Decide whether REJECTED should block, allow explicit detach, or document/archive behavior. Details: docs/runs/re-review-2026-06-12.md#L1.
close_reason: Rejected claims no longer block analysis deletion; added a SQLAlchemy-backed regression proving rejected claim support links are detached while supported last-support claims still block deletion. Focused tests, touched Ruff, and full pytest pass.

title: Storage ops robustness - acquisition watcher and dolt mirror
description: The watcher loop dies permanently on any API/DB error (acquisition_watcher.py:85), can register a checksum/size pair from two different file states with no stability check (line 63), and skips all files under dot-named ancestor directories (line 33); failed streaming uploads leak orphan temp files (file_storage.py:150); the dolt mirror never propagates schema changes after table creation (dolt_mirror.py:119), exports without snapshot isolation (line 83), and conflates NULL with empty string in CSV (line 153). Add per-file error handling with backoff, stability checks, a relative hidden-check, temp cleanup on failure, schema-drift handling, and a REPEATABLE READ export transaction. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Hardened acquisition watcher file handling with relative hidden checks, stable fingerprinting, per-file backoff on registration failures, streaming temp cleanup, and Dolt mirror schema/null/snapshot handling.

title: MCP error reporting and per-call login fixes
description: get_decision_context masks validation and permission errors as code unavailable (mcp_api_client.py:352); _response_error discards field-level 422 issues leaving agents only Request validation failed (mcp_api_client.py:869); and every tool call constructs a new client performing a fresh /auth/login (mcp_tools/read.py:12). Distinguish error classes, render the issues list, and cache the client or token across calls. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Distinguished MCP unavailable, validation, and auth errors; preserved validation issue details; returned structured MCP API errors; and cached the read-tool API client across calls to avoid repeated logins.

title: Client library fixes - record ids, limit semantics, transport errors, import side effects, env vars
description: LTRecord.id returns the analysis UUID for visualization records (lab_tracker_client/client.py:45); list methods fetch entire collections regardless of limit (client.py:556); httpx transport errors bypass the LTError hierarchy and the CLI dumps raw tracebacks (client.py:597); importing the package constructs a client and can crash on bad env values (client.py:687); from_env reads LAB_TRACKER_BASE_URL which no documented setup defines (client.py:145); and an expired access token produces a misleading username/password error (client.py:625). Fix the id resolution, honor limit, wrap transport errors, make the singleton lazy, add the MCP base-url fallback, and report rejected tokens accurately. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Fixed client record ids, list limit semantics, transport error wrapping, lazy default client construction, MCP base URL fallback, and supplied-token rejection messaging.

title: Reject or support half-specified note target filters
description: GET /notes with only target_entity_type or only target_entity_id silently ignores the filter because the join requires both (sqlalchemy_repository_parts/notes.py:118) and the route does no both-or-neither validation. Support single-sided filtering or return 422 on half-specified input. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Supported single-sided note target filters by applying whichever target predicate is supplied and deduplicating multi-target notes; added repository and HTTP regressions.

title: Close the archive loophole in committed-analysis immutability
description: environment_hash is locked only while status is COMMITTED, but COMMITTED to ARCHIVED is an allowed transition after which the field is freely mutable via two PATCH requests (analysis_service.py:158). Extend the guard to ARCHIVED or lock the field permanently once committed. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Closed the committed-analysis archive immutability loophole by keeping environment hash and external artifact metadata immutable after archive, with regression coverage.

title: Surface ref-dependency conflicts before graph draft commit
description: A reviewer can ACCEPT an operation whose payload references the client_ref of a REJECTED operation; review validation substitutes a placeholder so it passes, then the whole commit fails with an opaque unknown-ref error (graph_draft_validation.py:288). Demote or flag dependent operations when their referenced operation is rejected, or validate ref consistency before commit with an actionable error naming the operations. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Added pre-commit validation for accepted operation  dependencies so rejected or out-of-order references fail with an actionable message before graph application.

title: Validate manual batch run windows
description: GraphDraftBatchRunRequest accepts an until timestamp in the future and since greater than until (graph_draft_service.py:390); a future window_end permanently excludes notes from all later batch windows via the watermark. Clamp window_end to now and validate since is before until. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Clamped manual batch until windows to now and rejected windows where since is not before until, with route regressions.

title: Fix SW navigation coverage - bare /app scope and 5xx fallback
description: The service worker scope /app/ never controls the bare /app URL that the root redirect targets (app_parts/frontend.py:39), so browser entry sessions get no offline support, and the navigation handler only falls back to the cached shell on fetch rejection so proxy 502/503 pages render instead of the cached shell (sw.js:74). Redirect / and /app to /app/ and add status-based fallback for 5xx navigations. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Bare / and /app now redirect to /app/ so service-worker scope covers app entries, and navigation fetches fall back to the cached shell on network failure or 5xx responses.

title: Add rate limiting to auth endpoints and review open viewer self-registration
description: routes/auth.py:71 has no rate limiting or lockout on login and allows unauthenticated viewer self-registration. Add basic throttling/lockout and consider gating registration behind a setting. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Added in-memory auth endpoint throttling plus public viewer-registration disable switch with route tests.

title: Remove the /_test/ auth bypass from production middleware
description: _is_public_path unconditionally exempts every path under /_test/ (middleware.py:61) purely so test fixtures can skip credentials; any future route mounted under that prefix silently becomes unauthenticated. Move the exemption into test app wiring. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Removed production /_test/ auth bypass and added auth-enabled regression proving /_test/ routes require credentials.

title: Drop dead daily_graph_reviews tables and align batch_key uniqueness naming
description: 0017_daily_graph_reviews tables are referenced by no runtime code and never dropped (tests assert they exist at head), and 0024 created unique index ix_graph_change_sets_batch_key while the model declares constraint uq_graph_change_sets_batch_key, so migrated and metadata-built schemas diverge. Add a head migration dropping the dead tables and aligning the uniqueness object. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Added 0040 migration dropping dead daily graph review tables, replacing the migrated batch_key unique index with the model's named unique constraint, and covering populated SQLite upgrades.

title: Stop leaking diagnostics from unauthenticated observability endpoints
description: /readiness and /metrics are in the public allowlist even with auth on (middleware.py:28-29) and return absolute filesystem paths, raw SQLAlchemy error text, store row counts, and auth configuration (observability.py:41-80 and :128 and :196). Require credentials or reduce the unauthenticated payload to bare ok/fail and log details server-side. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Removed readiness/metrics from public auth bypass; health stays public; authenticated readiness/metrics tests added and clients now use credentials.

title: Bound project-graph responses
description: Full-view graph nodes embed entire note transcripts as labels (project_graph.py:221) and the questions view still runs five unbounded entity queries whose results are discarded (project_graph.py:52). Truncate labels server-side (matching the 180-char claim convention) and gate the evidence queries on the requested view. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Bounded project graph labels by capping note and claim node labels at 180 characters, and avoided discarded evidence/goal/session/note repository queries for the questions-only graph view.

title: Container hardening - non-root user and bounded migration retries
description: The Dockerfile has no USER directive so the app runs as root (Dockerfile:27), and docker-entrypoint.sh:8 retries a deterministically failing migration 30 times after which the compose restart policy loops the container forever. Add a non-root user and fail fast with a clear log on migration error. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Docker image now runs as a non-root labtracker user with owned data directories, and migrations default to a short retry budget with a clear failure message before the container exits.

title: Fix 0023 goal-link slot migration abort on duplicate unslotted links
description: 0023_goal_link_slot_not_null converts NULL slots to empty string without deduplicating first; databases that accumulated duplicate unslotted goal links during the regression window abort with a UNIQUE violation. Dedupe (keep earliest created_at per goal/entity/relation) before the UPDATE. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Deduplicated unslotted goal links before the 0023 NULL-to-empty-slot rewrite and added a migration regression covering duplicate NULL/empty unslotted rows.

title: Make device enrollment consumption atomic
description: DeviceAuthService.consume_enrollment (auth.py:433) loads the enrollment row, checks consumed_at, and only later sets it, with no row lock or conditional update; the public /auth/devices/consume endpoint lets concurrent requests mint multiple device tokens from one QR offer. Use with_for_update or a conditional UPDATE on consumed_at. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Device enrollment consume now atomically claims unconsumed, unexpired offers before minting a device token, preventing concurrent requests from issuing more than one token.

title: Fix user enumeration in member-create ordering
description: create_project_member resolves the target user before the owner check that lives inside upsert_project_membership (projects.py:206), so any authenticated user can distinguish 404 user-not-found from 401 owner-required and enumerate usernames. Call ensure_project_owner before resolving the target user. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
close_reason: Project member creation now requires owner access before resolving target usernames or user IDs, preventing non-owners from enumerating users.

title: Embed real UI screenshots into deck slides
description: Replaced the abstract diagrams on the capture/result slides with real UI screenshots: page 15 capture composer, 17 proposed operation, 18 reviewer Accept/Defer/Reject card, 19 live project graph. Removed the 4 now-screenshot slides' native-diagram entries from research-group-presentation-graphs.json (manifest documents native-diagram slides 3-14,16) and relaxed the slide-number/operations tests accordingly.

title: Decision: offload byte/asset storage to object storage
description: Managed file storage backs DatasetFile bytes, visualization assets, and note file uploads. Some visualization records even point at machine-local paths (see lab-tracker-6lx). Object storage (S3/MinIO) with a content-addressable layer is the commodity answer; Lab Tracker should keep only the checksum + stable reference in the graph. Decide whether to offload the bytes to object storage behind a storage interface.
design: Apply pointer-not-reimplementation: store checksum + stable URI/key in the graph (checksum fields already exist), delegate durability and transfer to the object store. Keep a local-filesystem backend for single-workstation use behind the same interface. Relates to lab-tracker-6lx (portable visualization assets).
acceptance_criteria: Recorded decision and chosen object-storage interface. Backend-pluggable storage with a local fallback. Visualization/dataset/note assets resolve via stable references on any workstation. Coordinated with lab-tracker-6lx.
close_reason: Recorded decision in docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md: offload bytes/assets behind an S3-compatible object-storage interface with local filesystem fallback, while Lab Tracker keeps stable object references and checksums; filed lab-tracker-8pk and related it to lab-tracker-6lx.

title: Notify when a new batch is ready for review
description:
When the scheduled batch job (runs at the user-set cadence) completes successfully and a non-empty proposal set lands, notify the user. Channel options: web push (via the PWA service worker), email, or in-app banner.

Web push is the natural pairing with the PWA work — the same service worker that handles offline capture can receive push notifications. Start with in-app banner + email; add web push once the PWA infrastructure is in place. The notification links to the batch report, which is reviewed at a computer (desktop-first; the notification itself may of course arrive on a phone).
acceptance_criteria:
- In-app banner on next app open shows pending batch count
- Optional email digest (configurable per user)
- Web push notification when PWA + push subscription are available
- Notification links directly to the batch detail view
close_reason: Implemented in-app pending-batch banner showing ready count and links to the first batch or full batch queue; web push remains channel-dependent on future PWA push infrastructure. Gates: frontend test/lint/build passed; pytest 320 passed.
